title: Bryson DeChambeau: American running out of options after LIV Golf collapse, says Rory McIlroy
article_text:
Rory McIlroy says the addition of Bryson DeChambeau to the DP World Tour next season would bring more "eyeballs" to the tour but feels the American is running out of options.

DeChambeau's competitive future is uncertain following the collapse of LIV Golf, with the two-time US Open champion last week saying he will approach his next move with "humility and respect".

The 33-year-old American can apply for DP World Tour membership based on his status as a recent major champion, which would offer him the chance to earn back his PGA Tour card for 2028.

"I think a name like Bryson DeChambeau and everything he brings with him, good and bad, he brings eyeballs, which is a good thing for tournaments," said McIlroy, who was pipped to the 2024 US Open in dramatic fashion by DeChambeau.

"Honestly, I'm certainly not in his shoes, and nor would I ever want to be but it doesn't seem like he's got many options.

"You know, if he wants to play competitive golf, it doesn't seem like he's got many options."

Northern Ireland's McIlroy was speaking to reporters in Dubai before the DP World Tour Championship as he chases a record-equalling eighth season-long title.

The six-time major winner trails Spain's Eugenio Chacarra by 533 points in the Race to Dubai standings going into the final event in Dubai, which offers 2,000 points to the winner.

Nine players - Chacarra, McIlroy, Patrick Reed, Casey Jarvis, Aaron Rai, Jon Rahm, Ryan Fox, Jayden Schaper and Daniel Hillier - can still clinch the Race to Dubai title, but McIlroy would guarantee his fifth straight crown with victory at Jumeirah Golf Estates this week.

McIlroy's excellent record at the Dubai tournament includes three wins and a play-off defeat by England's Matt Fitzpatrick last year.

"I'm very excited to be back here, very excited to be in contention for the eighth," said the 37-year-old.

"I made some ground up last week, maybe not as much as I wanted, but I felt like it was a step in the right direction.

"Getting back to a place where I played, I played well and I had a lot of success, even last year in the play-off with Matt, it's been a course that's been very good to me over the years, and I have a lot of experience on it and a lot of experience up at the top end of the leaderboard."

An eighth Race to Dubai title would draw McIlroy alongside Colin Montgomerie, who won seven straight European Tour Order of Merit titles in the 1990s before adding an eighth in 2005.

With McIlroy chasing a fifth successive Race to Dubai title, he spoke about how proud he is of the "consistency" and "longevity" he has shown in his career.

"I think this will be the 15th or 16th year in a row that I will have finished the year in the top 10 in the world rankings," said the world number two.

"There may be a couple others that have done that before. Yeah, I'm very proud of that. I think that's maybe an underrated part of careers, is that longevity piece.

"I was very lucky to start so young and get my tour card at 18, and I've stayed pretty much injury-free throughout my career.

"And I've kept working and trying to get better at certain aspects of the game and always tried to see weaknesses or be critical of myself and try to get better at them."

title: GdS: The full story of Milan and Inter’s record-breaking €650m deal with Generali
article_text:
More details continue to emerge regarding the stadium naming rights deal between AC Milan, Inter and Generali.

La Gazzetta dello Sport write that even before it’s even been built, the new home of Milan and Inter is already the place to be. It’s no coincidence that Generali – the insurance giant – has decided to put its stamp on the façades, as was revealed last month at the presentation of the stadium.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The collaboration kicks off immediately. Generali are now the Official Insurance Partner of the two clubs. The stadium naming rights contract will last for 25 years and includes the payment of €50m until the stadium opens in 2031.

This includes €10m annually for each of the next five seasons, including the current one, to be split equally between Inter and Milan. Once the stadium is inaugurated, the sum will increase to €30m annually (€15m each) for the following 20 years. The total commitment amounts to €650m.

Generali wanted to associate its name with the stadium from the very beginning of this long journey, in order to establish itself in the collective imagination: it will only be the Generali Stadium, with no temporary or secondary names to muddy the waters.

Branding a stadium from day one – or rather, even before it opens – is particularly strategic in terms of marketing. For this reason, Generali have agreed to pay €10m a year for something that, for five years, will be on models and then on construction sites, but not yet in the experience of fans.

Moreover, the naming rights market still has ample room for development in Europe. A Kroll study of the 36 major European clubs highlighted this already in 2024: only 12 had sold the naming rights to their stadiums, for a total estimated potential value of €303m, equivalent to an average of €8.4m per season.

Italy and England were the leagues least inclined to this form of commercialisation, also held back by the historical connection between the stadiums and their names. In this scenario, the new Inter and Milan stadium represents a different opportunity: a stadium to be built around a commercial identity,.

It’s not just a sports sponsorship: it’s a key support for a project crucial to the next stage of development of the city, the beating heart of the country’s economy and finances. This explains the significant investment.

It was the first time Inter and Milan worked together on the same side of the table, to secure a commercial deal. Under the watchful eye of Oaktree and RedBird Capital, the two clubs’ Chief Revenue Officers – Giorgio Ricci and Maikel Oettle – took the lead in finalising the sale of the naming rights.

These will be transferred through Stadio San Siro, a company controlled by NSM Holding, equally owned by Milan and Inter. The Rossoneri and Nerazzurri had initially selected a small group of potential partners, focusing on major Italian companies.

This type of right is particularly attractive to companies with a strong interest in the local area. After an initial round of meetings, Generali was the company that immediately showed the most enthusiasm.

Inter and AC Milan thus decided to further discuss the deal with the insurance giant, finalising the contract within a few months, the largest ever signed by Generali in the sports sector. In addition to the price offered, a key factor was the partner’s status.

Who better than the insurance giant – with €4.3bn in net profit and €900bn in assets under management – can offer guarantees of solidity and solvency, especially in a long-term commitment?

The €650m is written in stone and represents a significant portion of the financial coverage for the entire real estate transaction. Moreover, thanks to the €50m ‘bridge’ payment, the clubs have the opportunity to cash in immediately.

A comparison with other major international stadiums further illustrates the scale of the operation. Once fully operational, with €30m annually, the Generali Stadium will rank at the top of the global naming rights market, becoming one of the most lucrative deals ever signed for a stadium.

In Europe, the benchmark is Spotify’s Camp Nou, which guarantees Barcelona €20m per season, while Bayern Munich earn around €13m annually from Allianz for the Munich Arena. London’s Emirates Stadium is currently worth an estimated €10-15m to Arsenal.

Atletico Madrid’s Riyadh Air Metropolitano is at a similar level to that of the Gunners. In Germany, Borussia Dortmund get around €11m for Signal Iduna Park. Juventus, with the Allianz Stadium, earns around €8-10m.

To find higher figures, one must look primarily to the United States, where the stadium sponsorship market is of a different size and characteristics. The Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles is worth approximately €31m annually, but the $700m twenty-year contract also includes other commercial activities of the AEG group and partnerships with the Lakers and Kings.

The same is true for SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles, whose twenty-year, $625m agreement equates to approximately €28m annually, but includes additional commercial components. Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, on the other hand, has signed a thirty-year agreement worth approximately $750m, equivalent to approximately €22m per season.

These transactions should be interpreted with caution, as the consideration does not always refer solely to the naming of the stadium. The Milan figure, however, is significant precisely because of the size of the naming rights component.

title: Bryson DeChambeau Announces Career News After LIV Golf Update
article_text:
Bryson DeChambeau took a heavy blow last week when LIV Golf confirmed it is shutting down.

LIV’s lawyers told a New Jersey bankruptcy court on Thursday that the league will wind down. The planned relaunch, known as LIV Golf 2.0, will not happen.

The 33-year-old had more star power than any other player backing LIV 2.0. He revealed he had no regrets about joining the league in 2022.

“I still believe in team golf,” he wrote.

The DP World Tour, formerly the European Tour, welcomed him with an offer, The Telegraph reported. Still, the news hit hard for a player who backed the league since 2022.

DeChambeau is expanding into the apparel business. He started with headcovers, partnering with SWAG Golf in April. Now he is slated to launch his own apparel collection.

DeChambeau announced a multi-year apparel partnership with SWAG on Monday, one day after his LIV statement.

“Headcovers were just the start… now I’m expanding my partnership with @swaggolfco into apparel!” he wrote, revealing the news.

The Bryson x SWAG collection launches Nov. 19 at SWAGGolf.com. At retail, it will sell only at Dick’s Sporting Goods and Golf Galaxy stores and their websites.

SWAG, based in Northbrook, said DeChambeau will wear its apparel at all professional competitions.

To mark the launch, SWAG and DeChambeau made 13 uniquely designed headcovers. DeChambeau believes it is the start of something special.

The DP World Tour offer could also open a path back to the PGA Tour. DeChambeau can take full 2027 playing privileges as a major champion.

The PGA Tour will switch to a Championship Series and a Challenger Series in 2028.

Rory McIlroy said last week he expects four DP World Tour players to earn Championship Series cards. He described the PGA Tour as leaning toward three and the DP World Tour toward five.

The current alliance between the tours runs through 2027. A new agreement must be in place for 2028.

DeChambeau faces a one-year PGA Tour ban after their last LIV appearance.

A top-10 Race to Dubai finish in 2027 could put him back on the PGA Tour in 2028. A suspended LIV player could, in theory, earn a Championship Series spot that way.

DeChambeau’s next scheduled start is the Nedbank Golf Challenge, set for Dec. 3-6 at Sun City in South Africa. He has not announced plans beyond that event.

title: Sabalenka wins WTA Finals opener despite wayward serve
article_text:
Aryna Sabalenka grappled with her own frustrations and a misfiring serve to begin her WTA Finals campaign with a tight victory over Karolina Muchova.

World number two Sabalenka is bidding to win the season-ending title for the first time in her sixth appearance.

With rival and world number one Elena Rybakina withdrawing on the eve of the competition, Sabalenka is arguably the favourite to triumph on the courts where she won the Indian Wells title in March.

However, neither she nor Wimbledon runner-up Muchova were consistently at their best in the first group two match.

Belarus' Sabalenka battled back from a break down in both sets to win 7-6 (7-2) 7-5.

She cut a frustrated figure at times but reined in her emotions, with her forehand in particular growing stronger as the match progressed.

Her serve, however, was inconsistent. Sabalenka produced seven double faults to four aces, but landed 59% of her first serves and won 33 of 44 points behind it.

"It was a bit tricky with the sun [and] with the shade," Sabalenka told Sky Sports.

"Sometimes I had to adjust my toss, sometimes I had to serve blind, but it's all part of the game."

French Open champion Mirra Andreeva was far more convincing in a 6-4 6-0 victory over Ukraine's Elina Svitolina later on Monday.

Sabalenka has had - by her high standards - a strange season.

For the first time since 2022 she has not won a Grand Slam singles title, having lost the Australian Open and US Open finals to Rybakina, and her last title came in Miami in March.

After winning just one of her three matches during the Asian swing, Sabalenka took a break before the season-ending finals.

She faced a tricky task against the crafty Muchova, who was the only player at the event to have a winning head-to-head against her.

The Czech also claimed the first break of the opening set - but, in a pattern that repeated throughout the match, Sabalenka broke straight back.

Muchova served for the first set but a string of errors forced her into a tie-break, and more mistakes gifted Sabalenka the opener.

A topsy-turvy second set featured five breaks of serve, with Sabalenka serving the match out on her second attempt.

Teenager Andreeva, who beat Sabalenka in the 2025 Indian Wells final, was ruthless against Svitolina.

The Russian reeled off seven games in a row against the wayward Svitolina, backed by her impressive backhand.

Andreeva saved all six break points she faced - four of which came in the final game - and hit nine winners to 12 unforced errors in a 77-minute victory.

Elsewhere, Britain's Cameron Norrie beat Australian James Duckworth 7-5 6-0 to reach the Stockholm Open second round.

Norrie will face top seed Taylor Fritz next as he continues his preparations for this month's Davis Cup Finals.

Fellow Briton Toby Samuel claimed a 6-3 6-2 win over Leo Borg - son of 11-time Grand Slam singles champion Bjorn - at the same event.

title: Real Madrid add Hotels.com as new global partner
article_text:
Spanish soccer giants Real Madrid have bolstered their commercial slate through a new global partnership with online travel agency and website Hotels.com.

Under the multi-year agreement, Hotels.com will gain a presence through matchday branding, digital content opportunities, and hospitality experiences at the LaLiga club’s iconic Bernabéu Stadium.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

As part of the deal, Hotels.com and Real Madrid will collaborate on campaigns to help supporters travel to matches, tournaments, and away fixtures, and showcase their rewards system through the club’s digital channel, in-stadium presence, and hospitality opportunities.

The deal expands Hotels.com’s presence in European soccer, having extended its multi-year tie-up with English Premier League champions Arsenal ahead of the 2026-27 campaign.

The deal, which builds on its original agreement struck in 2023, means Hotels.com retains a branding presence at the club’s Emirates Stadium home on men’s and women’s team matchdays, as well as on its social media and digital platforms.

The online platform also previously served as Tottenham Hotspur’s official accommodation partner as part of a four-year deal running from the 2018-19 through 2021-22 seasons.

For Real Madrid, the new deal adds to the club’s recent commercial activity, having added AI cloud computing firm Iren to its partnership slate as a global partner last month.

Real Madrid also brought in food delivery service Uber Eats as a new club partner in a three-season deal and renewed its tie-up with international sports marketing agency Sportfive, which will continue as an authorized VIP tickets partner for the Bernabeu.

A selection of key Real Madrid commercial partners includes Adidas (kit supplier), Emirates (front-of-shirt sponsor), and HP (sleeve sponsor).

title: Mars becomes official salty snacks provider for LA28 and Team USA
article_text:
Mars is expanding its presence in the Olympic and Paralympic movement after announcing a partnership with LA28 and Team USA, naming Cheez-It, Pringles, Club, Town House and Combos as the official salty snacks providers and proud supporters of the 2028 Games.

The agreement brings five brands from Mars Snacking’s portfolio into one of the world’s largest sporting platforms, creating opportunities to connect with consumers through the build-up to and delivery of the Los Angeles Olympic and Paralympic Games. The brands will look to engage fans through their established identities, with a focus on shared sporting experiences and celebrations around the Games.

Anton Vincent, President of Mars Snacking North America, said, “Working with LA28 and Team USA reflects Mars’ commitment to creating shared moments of connection through our iconic brands. We’re proud to bring Cheez-It® and Pringles® to the LA28 Games, giving fans more ways to celebrate every kind of greatness that makes the Games so meaningful — from the athletes competing on the world’s biggest stage to the fans cheering them on at home and sharing the journey, and snacks, together.”

John Slusher, CEO of U.S. Olympic and Paralympic Properties, added, “Watching the Games is an experience best shared, and nothing brings people together like incredible athletic moments and great snacks. Partnering with Mars Snacking to bring Cheez-It®, Pringles®, Club®, Town House® and Combos® to LA28 and Team USA gives fans across the country an authentic, flavorful way to experience American staples.”

Mark Marshall, Chairman of Global Advertising & Partnerships, NBCUniversal, continued, “The Olympic and Paralympic Games create shared experiences unlike anything else in media, bringing audiences together around moments that become part of our collective memory. Mars Snacking’s iconic portfolio has long been woven into those same moments in homes across America, and we’re excited to partner together to celebrate the athletes, stories and defining moments that will make LA28 unforgettable.”

The partnership adds to LA28’s expanding commercial portfolio as Los Angeles prepares to host the Olympic Games for the third time, following the 1932 and 1984 editions. The city will also stage its first-ever Paralympic Games.

For Mars, the agreement represents an opportunity to combine sports sponsorship, consumer engagement and media exposure around a global sporting event, extending the reach of its snack brands beyond traditional retail and advertising channels.

title: "Rolling maul banned" – Five controversial rugby law changes proposed for 2027
article_text:
The rolling maul could be heading for rugby's chopping block, with fresh calls to ban the tactic ahead of the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

New Zealand rugby writer Paul Lewis has had enough after watching the All Blacks beat Scotland 43-21 at Murrayfield.

Five of the ten tries in the match came from rolling mauls, including two of Scotland's three.

The Springboks weren't much different. Five of their nine tries against Italy came from the same tactic.

Writing in the New Zealand Herald, Lewis described the rolling maul as an increasingly predictable part of the game.

"World Rugby should ban it," he declared.

That's quite a statement. Somewhere in South Africa, a forwards coach has probably just spat out his morning coffee.

But the rolling maul isn't the only thing under fire.

Former referee Nigel Owens wants fewer replacements, while we've got a few suggestions of our own.

Here are five changes that could shake up rugby before the next World Cup.

These are proposals, not confirmed law changes for 2027.

Lewis believes the rolling maul has become an ugly spectacle, with teams repeatedly kicking penalties into the corner before driving over.

He argues it gives attacking players an unfair advantage because defenders cannot tackle the ball carrier through the bodies in front.

Writing in the New Zealand Herald, he called it "an affront to the principles of the game".

As reported by SA Rugby Magazine, Lewis has also suggested alternatives to an outright ban, including limiting mauls to 30 seconds.

RUCK verdict: I'm not convinced we should ban it completely. A perfectly executed rolling maul is still a thing of beauty. Unless you're defending it, obviously.

There's also something wonderfully brutal about watching eight forwards march their opponents backwards.

But a 30-second limit? I'd happily give that a go.

Nigel Owens has been banging this drum for years.

The former Test referee believes eight replacements are too many and has suggested reducing the number to four or five.

As Owens has previously argued, rugby would benefit from players having to last longer rather than coaches relying so heavily on tactical substitutions.

The thinking is simple. Tired forwards create space, and space creates tries.

It's certainly not something Rassie Erasmus will be rushing to support.

South Africa's famous Bomb Squad has turned the replacements bench into a weapon. Some opponents spend 50 minutes surviving the starting pack, only to discover another collection of enormous Springboks warming up.

RUCK verdict: I'd go with five replacements, provided we protect players and allow appropriate injury cover.

There's something appealing about seeing a 120kg prop trying to chase down a winger after 75 minutes.

Few things in modern rugby look quite as ridiculous as six enormous forwards lining up behind a ruck.

It resembles the queue for a beer at Twickenham, except everyone is wearing gumshields and there's considerably less desire to move forward.

Meanwhile, the scrum-half stands at the back, carefully preparing his box kick.

By the time he finally puts boot to ball, you could have made a cup of tea.

World Rugby already requires the ball to be played within five seconds of the referee calling "use it".

RUCK verdict: Scrap the caterpillar. If you want to box kick, get on with it.

Nobody buys a ticket to watch a human centipede shuffle backwards.

Rugby has already introduced the 20-minute red-card replacement into its laws.

But explaining the difference between the two types of red card to a casual supporter isn't particularly straightforward.

An orange card would mean the offending player leaves permanently, but their team can introduce a replacement after 20 minutes.

A traditional red would mean no replacement for the rest of the match.

Same basic sanctions, different colours.

It would also make decisions much easier to understand for supporters watching at home.

Imagine explaining to somebody watching their first rugby match that two players have both received red cards, but only one team will be allowed to replace theirs.

RUCK verdict: Rugby has enough complicated laws without making people guess what a red card actually means.

Give the 20-minute sanction its own colour.

Eight forwards going head-to-head is part of what makes rugby special.

What I don't love is watching the same scrum collapse four times while the clock keeps ticking.

Repeat until everyone has forgotten why the scrum was awarded in the first place.

After the first reset, stop the match clock until the ball goes in.

Referees would still have the authority to manage scrums safely, but teams wouldn't benefit from repeated resets eating away valuable seconds.

It's something worth trialling before the next World Cup.

RUCK verdict: Keep the scrum. Keep the contest.

Just stop letting two packs of forwards turn the final five minutes into a committee meeting.

Rugby doesn't need reinventing every five minutes.

Some of its greatest strengths are the things that make it different from other sports.

But that doesn't mean we should accept everything simply because we've always done it that way.

title: Jannik Sinner targets late-December comeback, keeps Australian Open 2027 in focus
article_text:
Jannik Sinner is targeting a return to competitive tennis in late December as he steps up his recovery from a persistent knee injury, with the Six Kings Slam in Saudi Arabia emerging as a possible first stop ahead of the 2027 Australian Open.

The Italian, who has been sidelined since winning the Wimbledon title in July, offered an update on his recovery at a event in Milan on Tuesday. While he is keen to return to the court before the new season, Sinner made it clear that he will not rush the process at the risk of aggravating his injury.

"The aim is to go to Australia, the aim is also maybe to do a couple of tournaments first. But I have to respect the protocols at the moment because if we rush things we could have more serious problems," Sinner said.

"I also only have that information, that I have to work hard every day for that objective and then we'll see."

The rescheduled Six Kings Slam in Riyadh is among the events Sinner is targeting as he looks to regain match fitness before the Australian Open. The exhibition tournament, which was initially scheduled for October, has been moved to December 27-30 amid security concerns in the Middle East. Sinner acknowledged that the event remains a possibility rather than a certainty, with the wider situation in the region also playing a part in the decision.

"That (is the target) but we all know the situation what's there at the moment, which is not the best, so this is not our decision as players, this is a more general decision," he said.

The Italian added that playing some matches before travelling to Australia could be beneficial, given that he has not competed since Wimbledon.

"But I think if we want to prepare for Australia (and) I'm not playing since Wimbledon, some matches before might be very helpful," he added.

The Six Kings Slam does not offer ATP ranking points but brings together some of the biggest names in men's tennis. Sinner won the previous edition and is expected to feature alongside Carlos Alcaraz,

, Alexander Zverev, Taylor Fritz and Alex de Minaur.

Sinner's last appearance came in the Wimbledon final in July, where he defeated Alexander Zverev to claim the fifth Grand Slam title of his career. However, a right knee problem subsequently forced him to miss several tournaments, including the US Open.

The prolonged recovery eventually led the 25-year-old to announce in October that he would not compete again in the 2026 ATP season. His extended absence also saw him lose the world No. 1 ranking, with Zverev taking over the top spot last week after Sinner's 95-week reign.

Sinner has reiterated that his priority is to return fully fit rather than risk a setback by making an early comeback. With the Australian Open scheduled for January, the late-December target could offer him an opportunity to get valuable match practice before the first Grand Slam of 2027.

title: Qualification process confirmed for the 2027 G4D Ryder Cup Presented by Ei Electronics
Six Nations and Sanzaar face new battle with World Rugby in bid to scrap relegation
article_text:
The Six Nations and Sanzaar are facing another battle with World Rugby over a desire from some unions to ensure that none of them can be relegated from the Nations Championship.

As reported last week by the Guardian, the 10 leading unions have set up a new company, F10, to run the Nations Championship and sell their broadcast and commercial rights for all competitions other than the World Cup, which remains the property of the global governing body, World Rugby.

The creation of F10 has led to concerns elsewhere in the sport that some of the 10 founding unions, particularly Wales and Italy, want to introduce guard rails protecting them from relegation to the second tier Nations Cup, which is run by World Rugby.

In another potential flashpoint there is a desire from the smaller unions, which is shared by World Rugby, for the Nations Cup commercial rights to be bundled with and sold alongside those of the Nations Championship, which would give them a right to a share of the proceeds.

While the Nations Championship has secured more than 80 broadcast deals for this year’s tournament in deals that were brokered before F10 was set up, the Nations Cup has brought in just 13, with games streamed on the World Rugby-owned RugbyPass TV in many markets, including the UK.

Japan and Fiji have been granted invitational status to play in the first three editions of the Nations Championship until 2030, when under the terms of the licence granted by World Rugby promotion and relegation has to be introduced.

The creation of the Nations Championship was approved only narrowly at a vote of the World Rugby Council in Paris before the 2023 World Cup final on the proviso that it would be an open league from 2030, with all sides able to be relegated and one promotion spot available to teams in the Nations Cup.

Sources present at the vote told the Guardian that any attempt to ringfence the 10 founding members in the Nations Championship would need to go to the council for approval, as it would represent a fundamental change to the conditions agreed three years ago and damage the integrity of the competition.

The original vote required a 75% majority to be passed and the motion received 41 votes for and 10 against, meaning it got a majority of 80%, so reopening the debate would be a risky move by the unions as it could throw the tournament into turmoil.

There has been a long power struggle between World Rugby and the unions over the Nations Championship, which was originally proposed by the governing body almost a decade ago but rejected as the unions refused to accept relegation. In addition World Rugby also originally suggested the joint sale of commercial rights, which the 10 biggest unions have now introduced themselves.

The Six Nations’ official position is that relegation will be brought in as originally envisaged in 2030, although they have also conceded that details over the precise mechanism remain to be determined.

Under World Rugby’s vision for growing the sport, the loser of the sixth v sixth Nations Championship playoff between the hemispheres in 2030 would be replaced by the winners of the Nations Cup.

Italy and Fiji are the lowest-ranked teams after four rounds of the inaugural Nations Championship, with Georgia and USA leading the way in the second-tier competition.

While Six Nations sources insist that negotiations over the size of parachute payment to be given to the relegated union to ensure their future financial sustainability is the main outstanding issue, individual unions are lobbying for exemptions.

Abi Tierney, the Welsh Rugby Union chief executive, said recently that it would be “‘cataclysmic” if Wales were relegated, while the Rugby Football Union chief executive, Bill Sweeney, declined to elaborate before last weekend’s matches on how relegation would be introduced.

“There’s a review group that has been set up by World Rugby and is chaired by Brett Robinson,” Sweeney said. “They’re looking at how the aspect of promotion and relegation can be set up. The basic premise is still the same, how that comes into effect needs to be sorted out.”

Mirra Andreeva broke a surprising six-month streak by beating Elina Svitolina at the WTA Finals
article_text:
Mirra Andreeva began her WTA Finals campaign with a straight sets victory against Elina Svitolina.

Andreeva dropped just four games as she romped to a 6-4, 6-0 win against the Ukrainian star in what is her first-ever appearance at the WTA Finals.

The Russian star has enjoyed a terrific season on the WTA Tour this year, which included her maiden Grand Slam success at Roland Garros and a career ranking high of world no 3.

Despite her resounding success in the 2026 season, there was one slightly worrying aspect to the star’s year and that was the lack of top 10 victories.

Prior to beating Svitolina, Andreeva had only won one match against a top 10 player in the 2026 season, which came against Iga Swiatek at the Women’s Stuttgart Open six months ago.

Speaking after the match to Christian’s Court, Andreeva also opened up about her difficulties against top 10 players during the 2026 season.

“I haven’t had a lot of top-10 wins this season, and to have one finally, it feels super, super nice,” said the Russian star, who will need to continue to improve that record if she wants to continue through the WTA Finals.

She will play Aryna Sabalenka and Karolina Muchova in her remaining round robin matches as she looks to qualify from her group and make the semifinals.

Andreeva also had revenge on her mind as she beat Svitolina in her opening round match, as the star had won their previous contest at the Australian Open.

“Honestly, all I was trying to think about was that she beat me in Australia earlier this year. I really tried not to think about the match we had last year on these courts,” said Andreeva during her on-court interview.

“Me and Conchita tried to prepare our best for this match. Of course I remember how I was playing when I beat her here, but I knew it would be a tricky match. She’s an amazing player. So I’m just very happy I was able to get through the match.”

Andreeva will be looking to reach her sixth WTA final at the WTA Finals and claim the fourth title of her season.

The Russian star has won the Linz Open, the Adelaide International, and Roland Garros and reached further finals at the China Open and the Madrid Open.

Winning the WTA Finals would see her overtake Sabalenka and become the world No 2 on the WTA Tour for the first time in her career, so there is plenty on the line for the talented teenager.

title: Get ready to ruck: Early bird tickets for HSBC SVNS Singapore 2027 on sale today

title: Lidl Expands Cycling Sponsorship Portfolio with Five Major Spanish Race Partnerships

Moreover, the brand has also collaborated with La Vuelta Femenina in an effort to embrace its “Feed Your Passion” philosophy by stressing the importance of fresh nutrition and physical activity.

Along with acting as the presenting partner and sponsor of the red jersey, Lidl has undertaken this project with the objective of creating awareness of women's cycling and encouraging equal rights in sports media.

Jens Thiemer, Chief Customer Officer Lidl Stiftung & Co. KG, said, “Cycling is part of everyday life and brings together many of the things Lidl stands for: conscious nutrition, an active lifestyle and genuine team spirit. That's why our commitment deliberately goes beyond traditional brand visibility. We want to bring our strengths as a company to the table, working together with our partners to further develop cycling and inspire as many people as possible to get active.”

Spanish races constitute yet another step in terms of Lidl's international dedication of Lidl towards the sport of cycling. In this case, Lidl goes far beyond the mere sponsorship model. The brand is going to use its resources as an international food retail company to cooperate with its partners and help develop events. The goal of cooperation is to make this sport accessible to a wide range of people.

title: NHL expands media rights agreement with RTL Deutschland for free-to-air coverage

NEW YORK – Starting November 30, RTL Deutschland will bring the National Hockey League (NHL) and its stars live to free-to-air TV. With NHL Monday Night Hockey, the NHL will regularly showcase additional games during European prime time, giving Germany’s passionate fan base more opportunities to watch live NHL action beyond weekends. NITRO viewers can look forward to live Sky Sport coverage of all 11 NHL Monday Night Hockey broadcasts this season, bringing NHL action to German audiences in prime time every Monday night, which will also be available on RTL+.

In addition to NHL Monday Night Hockey, RTL Deutschland will deliver live coverage of the NHL’s return to Germany with the 2026 NHL Global Series Germany presented by Kaufland, featuring the Ottawa Senators and Chicago Blackhawks at PSD Bank Dome in Düsseldorf on December 18 and 20. Both games will be broadcast live on NITRO, Sky Sport and RTL+. The renewed agreement also includes live coverage of the four NHL games scheduled to be played in Munich and Cologne during the 2027-28 season.

Inga Leschek, Chief Content Officer at RTL Deutschland: “In a media world where more and more content is available at any time, what is truly live and truly real becomes all the more valuable. Live sports create shared moments, emotions, and an immediacy that cannot be replaced. The NHL embodies this experience like no other league: fast-paced, intense, international, and featuring outstanding German stars. Germany is a strategic growth market for the NHL, and together we want to help spread this enthusiasm even more widely. With NHL Monday Night Hockey, we’re bringing the best hockey league in the world to free-to-air TV during primetime on a regular basis and making it easily accessible to even more people. And together, we will turn the NHL Global Series Games in Germany into celebrations of the game of ice hockey. The fact that we can combine RTL Deutschland’s enormous reach with Sky Sport’s sports expertise demonstrates the great potential of our joint venture—for the fans, for our partners, and for the sport.”

Frank Robens, Executive Vice President of Sports at RTL Deutschland: "RTL Deutschland and the NHL are going on a power play together. More German stars than ever before are currently playing in the world’s top hockey league, led by German superstar Leon Draisaitl. With NHL Monday Night Hockey and NHL Global Series Games on NITRO, we’re bringing them to German free-to-air TV on a regular basis during primetime and make this fascinating, fast-paced sport accessible to an even larger audience. Sky Sport is and will remain the long-term home of the NHL in Germany. Together, we’re now bringing the best of both worlds together: first-class sports coverage, maximum reach, and plenty of passion for ice hockey. I’m convinced this will inspire many new fans to get excited about the NHL.”

David Proper, NHL Chief Media Officer and Senior Executive Vice President: "The appetite for NHL hockey in Germany continues to grow, driven by passionate fans and the success of German players making an impact across our league. Expanding on our partnership with RTL Deutschland to showcase NHL Monday Night Hockey in prime time represents an important step in bringing the game to more households and strengthening our connection with fans throughout the country.”

Presenter Michael Leopold and pundit Patrick Köppchen will be hosting from the main studio in Unterföhring starting 20 minutes before the start of each match on NITRO and Sky Sport Mix as well as RTL+. title: Borthwick gets a glimpse of first-choice back three – before injuries strike again
article_text:
Rugby, at its heart, is a simple game. Win the collisions and you’ll more than likely win the match. Rule the skies, own the floor and the chances are you’ll end up on the right side of the ledger. Put square pegs in square holes and you can achieve the sort of attacking fluidity required for a record score against Australia. The complicated bit, once you stop trying to put them in round holes, is keeping those square pegs fit.

England’s emphatic win against the Wallabies on Sunday was the first time in two years Borthwick has been able to field a back three of Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, Tommy Freeman and George Furbank. It was also the first time they have lined up with 11, 14 and 15 on their respective backs.

It will not be the last but it was a fleeting glimpse nonetheless. Feyi-Waboso sustained an ankle injury that will rule him out for the rest of the autumn campaign. Furbank has a groin problem that will keep him sidelined against Japan, and given Borthwick is considering resting some players, it may be Freeman sits out on Saturday. It could conceivably be an entirely different back three against Eddie Jones’s side.

Given how serious it is, Feyi‑Waboso’s ankle injury was the major blot on England’s copybook against Australia. His time on the field was both a reminder of how devastating a runner he can be and how susceptible to injury he is. Feyi-Waboso’s handling was not perfect but it took him about 90 seconds to showcase the threat he possesses when scoring his disallowed try, cruising through a gap prised open for him by Fin Smith.

In his 40 minutes on the pitch Feyi-Waboso made 130 metres from his eight carries, demonstrating time and again how elusive he is. As Borthwick remarked after the win on Sunday, the game at present favours attacking sides who can keep making ground and keep recycling the ball, and in Feyi‑Waboso England have someone who will always ensure opposition defences are scrambling.

On the evidence of his showing against Australia and his previous outing against Argentina, it does not feel hyperbolic to say England become an entirely different proposition with the 23-year-old winger in the side. England’s attack coach, Lee Blackett, knows all about Feyi-Waboso’s threats from their time together at Wasps and with Smith purring as he did on Sunday, the fly-half has the ability to unleash Borthwick’s most dangerous runner.

The trouble is, it has not happened often enough since Feyi‑Waboso made his debut in early 2024. Now that he is out of the rest of England’s November Tests, he will have managed just 17 appearances in England’s 36 matches since and including his debut come the end of the year. A hamstring injury threatened his involvement this autumn, it was the same issue that forced him to miss the Six Nations and a shoulder problem that ruled him out of the Championship 12 months earlier. He has not managed to string together more than five consecutive starts for England in his career.

Furbank, meanwhile, made his first appearance for England on Sunday since the 2024 autumn victory against Japan. His run of bad luck with injuries has been astonishing – struck down by appendicitis when finally set to make his comeback over the summer – but the gracefulness with which he played against the Wallabies was a joy to watch. Wearing white boots to match his kit only added to the impression that Furbank glides across the pitch. His break to set up Jack van Poortvliet’s try was the champagne moment of an effervescent display, a reminder of what England have missed in his absence. The hope must be that he is fit to face the All Blacks on Saturday week.

Freeman’s “second debut” for England came in the same match in which Feyi-Waboso won his first cap, having been overlooked for the first 12 months of Borthwick’s tenure. He went on to cement his status of one of the world’s leading wings, before Borthwick persevered with attempting to reinvent him as an outside-centre. Given Freeman has started the past three matches back on the right wing, it seems common sense has won the day.

In the two years since they all last lined up together, England have tried all manner of combinations. Freddie Steward and Tom Roebuck enjoyed a degree of success when aerial supremacy was all the rage, but it does not feel like a coincidence that during England’s worst Six Nations campaign this year Feyi‑Waboso was injured throughout, Furbank was overlooked and Freeman was often deployed at centre. For the first defeat by Italy, not one of them appeared in the back three.

With 11 months before England’s World Cup opener against Tonga, however, Borthwick has his first‑choice back three combination now staring him in the face. The perfect blend of stylish playmaker at full-back, a robust, ultra‑consistent performer on one wing, a game-breaker on the other.

England’s budget does not stretch to the amount of cotton wool required to ensure they all make the plane to Australia next year, but there are echoes of the 2019 contingent of Elliot Daly, Anthony Watson and Jonny May with the current trio. If victory over a woeful Wallabies side told us anything it is that England have a set of outside backs to make the rest of the world sit up and take note once more, if they can all stay fit. The problem is it remains a big if.

title: Andreeva wins final seven games to beat Svitolina in FAGE WTA Finals singles debut
article_text:
Mirra Andreeva's FAGE WTA Finals singles debut was a winning one Monday at Indian Wells. The 19-year-old won the final seven games to defeat Elina Svitolina 6-4, 6-0 in 70 minutes.

The victory improved Andreeva to 1-0 in Group 2 play, joining Aryna Sabalenka atop the standings. It also improved her record against Svitolina to 2-1 and avenged her loss at this year's Australian Open.

"Honestly, I feel like I haven't had a lot of Top 10 wins this season. To have [another] one finally, it feels super nice," Andreeva told reporters. "I guess it was good that I didn't think about it, because I feel like the less I think the better it is. But I'm just super happy I was able to get a win against such an experienced player."

One of the match's main storylines was the experience gap between Andreeva, 19, and Svitolina, the 2018 champion. They entered as the players with the largest age gap (12 years, 229 days) to face one another at the year-end championships since Venus Williams and Caroline Garcia in 2017.

In the end, youth prevailed as Andreeva became the fourth higher seed to win in the first four matches of this year's singles event, joining Sabalenka (vs. Karolina Muchova), Linda Noskova (vs. Marta Kostyuk) and Coco Gauff (vs. Jessica Pegula).

4: It's the fourth time since the format's reintroduction in 2003 that all four higher seeds have won their opening round-robin matches, joining 2009, 2012 and 2024. Potential good news for No. 3 seed Andreeva? In both 2012 (Serena Williams) and 2024 (Gauff), the No. 3 seed went on to win the title.

7: Andreeva held serve throughout a match for the seventh time this season. She saved all six break points she faced against Svitolina, including four in the final game.

51: Only Elena Rybakina (54) has claimed more WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz wins this season than Andreeva (51).

87: Andreeva won 87% of her first-serve points in the opening set, ensuring the break she secured on a Svitolina double fault for 3-2 was all she needed to claim the opener.

603: Andreeva defeated Sabalenka in their most recent meeting 603 days ago in the 2025 Indian Wells final. The title made her the third-youngest champion in tournament history behind Martina Hingis (1998) and Serena Williams (1999).

Sabalenka owns a 4-2 lead in the head-to-head.

After the victory over Svitolina, Andreeva sought extra time on the practice court as she looks to chip away at that deficit.

"It actually was my initiative," Andreeva said. "I think it's the very first time that I asked Conchita (Martinez) to go to the practice courts. I think something's wrong, like I'm aging. I don't know, something is going on. So she was very surprised. She was like, 'Are you kidding?'

"She didn't believe me, because usually that doesn't happen often. But I just wanted to clean my shots. I wanted to serve a little. I just wanted to feel a bit more free on the court, and that was the purpose behind it."

Mediapro extends Prime Video NBA production contract

Mediapro, the Spanish sports production and rights agency, has renewed its Spanish-language production tie-up with the Amazon Prime Video streaming service for its coverage of North American basketball's top-tier NBA in Spain and Latin America.

Through an extension unveiled today, Mediapro is continuing to support the production of over 200 NBA games across the 2026-27 season. The deal covers Spain and Spanish-language markets in the Americas, including the US.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The deal means that production, coverage, reception, and transmission of these 200 games are managed from Mediapro studios in both Spain and Mexico. This approach involves collaboration with Prime Video, enabling coverage to be tailored to local audiences.

This extension has been formally announced with the 2026-27 NBA having begun on October 20. It follows the initial deal between the NBA and Mediapro, announced in September last year.

Prime Video has also become the NBA’s strategic partner and third-party global destination of NBA League Pass – the league’s DTC subscription service, with expanded distribution rights for the platform in the US and internationally.

In terms of recent Mediapro rights activity, this month has already seen the agency extend a production and distribution agreement with South American soccer's governing body CONMEBOL through 2030.

The company will take responsibility for producing and distributing the international feed for around 700 matches a year, plus the on-site production of every match played in Bolivia.

On January 1, meanwhile, Mediapro will rebrand as Imagina. The decision was unveiled in mid-September, with the group's parent company carrying the same name.

title: British Cycling appoints Pitch Marketing Group
article_text:
British Cycling has appointed Pitch Marketing Group as lead creative agency to promote the 2027 Grands Départs of the Tour de France and Tour de France Femmes avec Zwift.

It will create an integrated, multi-channel awareness campaign that runs in the UK from early next year, working with British Cycling’s Grand Départ GB team and communications agency SPECTACLE. The aim is to get millions of spectators to the roadside across Scotland, England and Wales and to create a “summer of cycling”.

The campaign will also promote JOY, the social impact programme attached to the Grands Départs. JOY focuses on health and wellbeing, skills development and community connection, and includes a national volunteer programme.

Britain will be the first country outside France to host the starts of both races in the same year, and the women’s race will visit for the first time. The men’s race begins in Edinburgh on 2nd July 2027, with three stages taking in Carlisle, Keswick, Liverpool, Welshpool and Cardiff. The women’s race starts in Leeds on 30th July 2027, visits Manchester and Sheffield, and finishes its Grand Départ with a team time trial in central London on 1st August 2027.

Pitch was founded in 2002 by Chief Executive Henry Chappell and works with brands, rights holders, media companies and major events across sport.

Esha Glen, Marketing Lead for Grand Départ GB 2027, said, “Following a highly competitive pitch process we are delighted to be working with Pitch to bring to life their exciting vision for the promotion of the Tour de France and Tour de France Femmes avec Zwift next year. Pitch’s team really captured the sense of excitement we want to create to engage and inspire the broadest possible audiences. The Grands Départs 2027 will be an incredible free-to-attend roadside spectacle taking place across Britain. We want to see as many fans on the roads as possible and, with Pitch’s help, to make 2027 the summer of cycling.”

Henry Chappell, Chief Executive of Pitch Marketing Group, said, “Britain has an amazing track record of staging the world’s biggest sporting events, and we are incredibly thrilled to be playing a part in the return of the Tour de France to the UK. As well as being an event that will create memorable moments for millions of spectators, it is a great opportunity to promote the sport of cycling to younger audiences. And it is another incredible national occasion to elevate women’s sport. We are looking forward to seeing millions of Brits bringing the atmosphere to cheer on the world’s best cyclists and witness one of sport’s most spectacular events in person.”

Henry Chappell is a longstanding member of the Sport Industry Group network, attending the SIAs and most recently joining the jury for the inaugural Sport Industry Hall of Fame.

title: Jaguar TCS Racing signs Elysia as partner
article_text:
Jaguar TCS Racing has signed a partnership with Elysia by Fortescue Zero, naming the company as its battery intelligence partner ahead of the Formula E World Championship’s GEN4 era.

Elysia combines battery physics, systems engineering and probabilistic AI to manage battery risk and improve performance in automotive, heavy industry and energy storage. Fortescue Zero will use the partnership to feed lessons from racing into its next generation of products, as Jaguar enters the new era with the Jaguar I-Type 08.

The deal builds on an existing relationship with Jaguar’s parent company. JLR has used Elysia since May 2024 in developing its next generation of electric vehicles, with the aim of improving battery longevity, safety and performance. Jaguar says technology tested on track has fed into the development of the Jaguar Type 01, its all-electric four-door GT, which launched in October.

Jaguar TCS Racing is Formula E’s most successful team, with 26 wins and 63 podiums since its debut in 2016. It won the Teams’ title in 2024, when Jaguar also took the inaugural Manufacturers’ Trophy. Drivers António Félix da Costa and Stoffel Vandoorne are both former Drivers’ World Champions. Jaguar will also supply its GEN4 powertrain to the Envision and Fortescue Zero Racing teams.

The 2026/27 calendar includes Formula E’s first races at Brands Hatch, as well as new rounds at the Circuit of the Americas in Austin and at Zandvoort.

Ian James, Team Principal at Jaguar TCS Racing, said, “We are delighted to welcome Elysia by Fortescue Zero as our Battery Intelligence partner as we embark on an exciting new era of Formula E.“

“Technical innovation will be critical to success in this new chapter of Formula E, and what makes this partnership particularly exciting is the opportunity to demonstrate how innovation developed through the demands of motorsport can drive meaningful benefits beyond the race track.“

Tim Engstrom, Managing Director at Elysia, said, “Formula E is one of the toughest proving grounds for battery technology in the world. Every second, every charge and every percentage of battery performance matters.“

“That is what makes this partnership so exciting. Jaguar TCS Racing has the ambition to innovate and drive technical leadership for success on track and for customers on the road.“

“In motorsports, speed and teamwork is everything. At Elysia, we bring that same approach, with our engineers working to test ideas, turn battery insights into decisions and rapidly put improvements into practice.“

title: Rush Sports picks up NBA rights in the Caribbean
article_text:
Rush Sports, the pay-television network owned by Caribbean Premier Sports Limited (CPSL), has secured a package of rights in the region to North American men's basketball’s NBA.

Through the agreement, live NBA games will be available across 24 Caribbean markets on Rush Sports channels.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Throughout the season, Rush Sports will show a selection of live games from the regular-season, playoffs, and the Conference Finals series.

The network will broadcast live games on Mondays and/or Tuesdays, together with selected Sunday nights beginning in February, 2027.

Additional shoulder programming will include player and team features, Caribbean-focused stories, regular tune-in information, and special coverage around key NBA moments.

The main package of NBA rights in the region is held by media giant NBCUniversal through its 11-year deal with the league covering multiple territories.

The NBA features several players with Caribbean roots, including VJ Edgecombe (Philadelphia 76ers), Buddy Hield (Chicago Bulls), and Deandre Ayton (Washington Wizards) from the Bahamas and Jose Alvarado (New York Knicks) from Puerto Rico.

“Through this collaboration with CPSL, we are bringing live NBA action to more fans across the Caribbean than ever before.”

title: RTL to provide FTA NHL coverage through Sky Deutschland deal
article_text:
North American ice-hockey's NHL is set to receive free-to-air (FTA) coverage in Germany for the remainder of the 2026-27 campaign, via a deal expansion between the league and commercial broadcaster RTL Deutschland.

Through a tie-up unveiled today, RTL will air 'Monday Night Hockey' every week in European primetime for the rest of the season, on its Nitro FTA channel.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

All 11 Monday Night Hockey games until the end of the campaign will be shown on Nitro, with this news coming following RTL's acquisition of pay-TV giant Sky Deutschland, which had a pre-existing deal in place to be the NHL's existing main partner in the DACH region.

RTL's deal to take over Sky was confirmed in early June, and involved RTL paying an "upfront cash consideration" of €68 million ($79.2 million at the time) to Sky Deutschland's owner up to this point, US heavyweight media entity Comcast.

The first Monday Night Hockey game under the terms of this deal comes on November 30, as the Ottawa Senators – featuring Germany's Tim Stutzle – take on the Nashville Predators (at 6:45 PM local time for a German audience).

In addition, RTL will provide live coverage of the two regular-season NHL games set to take place in Germany next month, as well as the four games scheduled for 2027-28 in that market.

The NHL Global Series Germany (presented by Kaufland, through a deal announced last week) will see the Senators play two games in Dusseldorf against the Chicago Blackhawks, on December 18 and 20.

Both events will be shown live by Nitro, the RTL+ digital streaming service, and also by Sky.

The quartet of 2027-28 Germany NHL games, meanwhile, will take place across Munich and Cologne, with teams yet to be determined.

The Sky Deutschland-NHL deal is a long-term affair that was unveiled in May 2025. It entails Sky airing over 300 NHL games live per campaign, including the post-season playoffs and Stanley Cup final coverage.

Around one-third of the total number of contracted NHL players are European, with the DACH region specifically one of the league's specific targeted growth areas.

David Proper, chief media officer and executive vice president at the NHL, said: "Expanding on our partnership with RTL Deutschland to showcase NHL Monday Night Hockey in prime time represents an important step in bringing the game to more households and strengthening our connection with fans throughout the country."

In terms of recent NHL activity in Germany, the Kaufland tie-up sees the brand become the league's official grocery retail partner in Germany, Czechia, and Slovakia, in addition to the presenting sponsorship element.

Late last month, meanwhile, the NHL unveiled a major agreement – Europe-wide – with global logistics and delivery giant DHL.

That deal covers the Germany games, as well as a pair of games taking place in Finland later this month, featuring the Carolina Hurricanes and Seattle Kraken.

title: Wainwright gives Wales injury scare for All Blacks
article_text:
Number eight Aaron Wainwright has emerged as a major injury concern for Wales' Nations Championship game against New Zealand in Cardiff on Saturday.

The 29-year-old picked up a leg injury and has since been seen in a protective boot. He did not train on Tuesday.

Head coach Steve Tandy will name his team on Thursday and the absence of the former Dragons player would be a major blow.

Wainwright started in the 28-21 victory against Japan last Saturday and was the most experienced forward in the squad.

The Leicester number eight, who was winning his 71st cap, is also Wales' most effective forward ball-carrier.

New Zealand wing Will Jordan will miss the game because of a hamstring injury but centre Jordie Barrett is available for selection to face Wales after passing his head injury assessment (HIA) protocols.

Recalled Taine Basham would be the leading contender to replace Wainwright on Saturday, with Scarlets back-rower Taine Plumtree providing the other option in the squad.

Basham was rewarded with a squad call-up having been the form number eight in Welsh domestic rugby this season.

The Cardiff number eight has not played for Wales since the 2024 Six Nations, while his previous start to that was in 2022.

After the All Blacks match, Wales will host Australia on 21 November, before the Nations Championship finals weekend at the end of the month, hosted by the Allianz Stadium at Twickenham.

Wales currently lie fifth out of sixth in the northern hemisphere table after two wins from four matches.

Wales assistant coach Dan Lydiate says Wainwright has not been completely ruled out yet but accepts he could miss the weekend's action.

"He picked up a bit of a knock, it's a minor injury and he's walking around in a boot at the minute, but it's more precautionary," said Lydiate.

"We've been lucky enough with Wainwright that he's been quite robust over the years. The medical staff are working as quick as they can to turn him around.

"I don't know if he'll be available this week, but they're doing everything in their power to make sure he is."

Lydiate recognised the significance of Wainwright's potential absence but backs the squad's depth.

"If that is the case, it will give someone else an opportunity, and you never know, we might find the next Aaron Wainwright."

title: Carlos Alcaraz hits milestone achievement which it took Roger Federer seven years longer to achieved
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz achieved yet another career first at the Paris Masters, by winning the indoor ATP 1000 event for the first time in his glittering career.

The Spaniard defeated the likes of Casper Ruud, Taylor Fritz, and Alex Michelsen, before beating Ben Shelton in straight sets to lift the trophy.

Alcaraz has now won seven out of nine of the Masters 1000 titles on the ATP Tour, with just the Canadian Open and the Shanghai Masters trophies eluding him.

As a result of his victory at the Paris Masters, Alcaraz has become just the fifth man in tenis history to claim both Roland Garros and the Paris Masters in the French capital.

The Spaniard has also managed the feat at a significantly younger age than the other four players who have achieved the feat.

Alcaraz joins Andre Agassi, Novak Djokovic, Alexander Zverev, and Roger Federer, who have all won the Paris Masters and Roland Garros in their careers.

Agassi, Djokovic, and Zverev all managed the feat at 29 years old, while Federer landed the achievement at 30 years old, which makes it even more impressive that Alcaraz has managed the feat at just 23.

Jannik Sinner has the chance to earn the achievement at 25 years old if he wins Roland Garros this year, which just goes to show how impressive Alcaraz’s latest achievement is.

Alcaraz had previously struggled at the Paris Masters too.

Prior to his 2026 success, the star had failed to get past the quarterfinals and had two second round exits to his name from his first five appearances.

He now has the chance to achieve another first-time achievement at the ATP Finals, as he looks to win the year-end tournament for the first time in his career.

He reached the final of the tournament for the first time in his career in 2025, but he was beaten by Sinner.

With no Sinner at the tournament this year, Alcaraz will be one of the overwhelming favourites to win the tournament in 2026.

The Spaniard seems to have shrugged off his issues at indoor tournaments and he seems significantly fresher than his ATP rivals at this point in the season, likely due to his four and a half month break due to the wrist injury he suffered at the Barcelona Open in April.

The ATP Finals takes place between the 15th and 22 November.

title: 8 Big Names Missing The 2026 DP World Tour Championship
article_text:
It's a huge week at Jumeirah Golf Estates as the DP World Tour Championship marks the end of a memorable season.

Eugenio Chacarra holds a slender lead with just one event left in the Race to Dubai, with big names like Rory McIlroy, Patrick Reed and last week's winner Jon Rahm chasing him down.

The action gets underway on Thursday on the famous Earth Course as many big names hope to mount a challenge for the trophy, but a number of notables have either opted to stay at home or haven't managed to qualify.

The top 50 in the rankings are eligible for the tournament, which adds extra spots when players withdraw. It means Joost Luiten, sitting 56th, has made it into the field due to the number of players sitting it out.

So, which big names are missing the 2026 DP World Tour Championship? Let's take a look...

World No.3 Matt Fitzpatrick revealed at the BMW PGA Championship that he was "not comfortable" travelling to the Middle East amid the ongoing tensions in the region.

The Englishman became a father in August and said that was a key cause for why he was considering to stay at home.

At 14th in the rankings, the 2022 US Open champion would have been in with a chance of winning the Race to Dubai had he played well in Abu Dhabi last week.

He has won this week's event at Jumeirah Golf Estates three times, a record he shares with Rory McIlroy.

Justin Rose is another big-name Englishman who has opted to miss the DP World Tour Play-Offs.

Rose likely would have got into the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship last week but does not qualify for the season-ender at 75th in the rankings.

The 2013 US Open champion last played in India, where he finished T42nd.

The 46-year-old currently ranks 20th in the world after winning this year's Farmers Insurance Open in record-breaking fashion, which he followed with a T3 at The Masters.

Shane Lowry has qualified for this week's event at 20th in the Race to Dubai rankings.

Lowry, who won the Irish Open in September by an incredible 11-stroke margin, has not spoken publicly on his reason for skipping both Abu Dhabi and Dubai but we assume it is due to the conflicts in the region.

Like Rose, Lowry last played at the DP World India Championship, where he finished T15th.

Another big name missing who was qualified for the season-ender is Min Woo Lee.

The Australian currently sits 48th in the rankings but has decided to skip the Play-Offs after a strong finish to his PGA Tour season where he finished T4th in the FedExCup.

Lee ranks 30th in the world after two runners-up finishes and a third-place this year.

Ludvig Aberg currently ranks 53rd in the Race to Dubai standings but was eligible for the tournament due to the likes of Fitzpatrick, Lowry and Lee opting to skip the week.

However, he has done the same by ending his DP World Tour season in Madrid at the Open de Espana, where he was a solid T7th.

The Swede finished T3rd here at Jumeirah Golf Estates last year so would have been among the tournament favorites.

Robert MacIntyre also decided to skip the Play-Offs, and at 61st in the rankings he would have needed a strong finish in Abu Dhabi to make the top 50.

The Scot, who became a father for the first time this year, decided to stay at home due to the ongoing tensions in the Middle East.

It means misses the DP World Tour Championship for the first time since 2018.

He is set to play next at the Hero World Challenge in The Bahamas next month.

Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen is currently battling to retain his card on the PGA Tour after earning status last year via the DP World Tour. He is 51st in the Race to Dubai standings so would have made it into the field.

The talented Dane, who won the Australian Open in December, finished T3rd at the DP World Tour Championship in his debut last year.

He currently sits 108th in the FedExCup Fall rankings, with the top 100 earning their cards for 2027.

Viktor Hovland has not played since September's Open de France and he has only appeared four times on the DP World Tour this year.

He was due to play in the DP World India Championship after finishing 2nd in the FedExCup standings, but withdrew without explanation on Monday of the tournament week after being one of the headline names announced in the field earlier this year.

At 102nd in the rankings he was ineligible for the Play-Offs. It is unknown when his next start will be.

title: USA Sports and the Horse Racing League (HRL) Announce Partnership to Air All Three Inaugural Race Days Live on USA Network in Spring 2027 – Company Announcement

“USA Sports is the ideal partner for HRL as we focus on broadening fan interest in our league and attracting new and younger demographic to horse racing,” said Greg Maffei, Executive Chairman of HRL. “Our vision of bringing more storytelling, deeper connections with teams, personalities and our equine athletes that run these races is going to become a reality based in part on USA Network’s ability to reach people not just on television but on other social media platforms.”

Added Danny Epstien, CEO of HRL, “USA Sports understands the value of our content and the need to leverage that in unique and different ways. We are thrilled to have them as our partner as we launch HRL.”

Last week, HRL announced the appointments of Renee Wilm as Chief Business Officer, J-T Ladt as Chief Marketing Officer and Clifford Lidell as Chief Brand Officer, and named Elevate, the award-winning global sports and entertainment agency, as its exclusive partner for ticketing, hospitality and sponsorship sales.

title: Wales confirm injury blow as update provided and likely replacement emerges
article_text:
Wales have confirmed that Aaron Wainwright is likely to miss Saturday's Nations Championship with the All Blacks.

WalesOnline reported earlier on Tuesday that the 29-year-old was a major doubt for the visit of New Zealand to Cardiff this weekend, with Taine Basham likely to make his first Welsh start in over four years. Having been in a protective boot on Monday, Wainwright was once again wearing it on Tuesday - taking no part in training.

Speaking on Tuesday afternoon, contact skills coach Dan Lydiate confirmed Wainwright was a doubt for Saturday's match.

"He picked up a bit of a knock at the weekend," said Lydiate. "I think it’s a minor injury.

"He’s walking around in a boot at the minute, but that’s more precautionary. The medical staff are assessing him and working as quickly as they can to turn him around.

"I don’t know if he’ll be available this week, but they’re doing everything in their power to make sure he is, if they can turn him around."

The 71-cap No. 8 has established himself as a key figure under Steve Tandy.

He has been started in 10 of the Wales head coach's 13 matches in charge, including the last seven.

While Lydiate admitted it was a blow, he added that it would give a chance for someone else to step up.

"I don’t know how many Test caps he’s got for us now, but he’s such a leader in terms of his ball-carrying ability," said the former back-row. "He’s up there now and he’s made a good impact.

"A quality player like Aaron Wainwright is a loss when he’s not available for us, but it gives someone else another chance.

"Touch wood, we’ve been lucky that Wainwright has been quite robust over many years, given the position he plays. Like anyone, you want your best players on the field.

"Teams in England have obviously looked to scout him, as they have some of our other world-class players, because they want our best players.

"He could potentially be a loss, but if that’s the case, it’ll give someone else an opportunity. You never know, we might find the next Aaron Wainwright."

Basham would appear to be the next cab off the rank, with WalesOnline understanding he's set to start.

It is over two years since his last Wales cap, while you have to go back to the 2022 Six Nations for his last Wales start.

However, having started the season strongly at No. 8 for Cardiff, he will get a second chance in the jersey at Test level - having only started at the back of the scrum once before, against Fiji in 2021.
