title: Ali Price gets Scotland call as veteran handed chance to end 2-year wait
article_text:
Experienced scrum-half Ali Price has been recalled to the Scotland squad ahead of Sunday’s Nations Championship clash with Australia.

The 33-year-old replaces Gus Warr, who has headed back to Sale Sharks after being drafted into Gregor Townsend’s group last week.

Price has not played for Scotland since starting against Fiji in November 2024 but has forced his way back into contention following an impressive run of form with Montpellier, who sit third in the French Top 14.

He joins Ben White, George Horne and Jamie Dobie among Townsend’s eye-catching scrum-half options as Scotland look to bounce back from last weekend’s 43-21 defeat to New Zealand.

White started at nine against the All Blacks before being replaced by Horne in the second half, while Dobie was deployed on the wing and now more changes could be afoot.

Warr, who has won two Scotland caps, was not included in the original squad for the autumn campaign before being called in to train last week.

Price will now hope his club form can propel him towards a first Scotland appearance in two years.

title: "Not great" - Will Jordan remains stood down after 'worrying' injury update
article_text:
The All Blacks have been handed a fresh injury concern ahead of their clash with Wales, with Will Jordan facing an anxious wait over a suspected hamstring problem.

The electric outside back suffered the injury during New Zealand's 43-21 victory over Scotland at Murrayfield on Saturday.

Jordan was unable to finish the contest, leaving the All Blacks sweating over his availability for the remainder of their November campaign.

And the latest update from assistant coach Tana Umaga doesn't sound particularly encouraging.

Speaking to Herald Now on Monday, Umaga admitted the early signs weren't promising.

"Yeah, no, not great, I'd say at this stage, but it's still early," he said.

"We've got to get the appropriate scans and medical checkups as much as we can to see where he's at."

Those comments suggest New Zealand could be without one of their most dangerous attacking weapons when they face Wales this weekend.

However, the full extent of Jordan's injury remains unclear, with the All Blacks yet to confirm a recovery timeline.

Jordan's pace, finishing ability and knack for finding space make him a particularly difficult player to replace.

Losing him would be another headache for the All Blacks, who are also monitoring Jordie Barrett following his failed head injury assessment against Scotland.

With Wales next on the schedule, New Zealand's medical team have some important decisions ahead.

For now, Jordan's involvement remains uncertain. And judging by Umaga's comments, All Blacks supporters have every reason to be concerned.

Jordan has spent years making defenders look like they're running through treacle. Now it's his own hamstring threatening to slow him down.

title: Glasgow Warriors begin search for managing director with Kenny Brown to step down
article_text:
Kenny Brown will step down as Glasgow Warriors managing director at the end of next month.

Brown has been part of Glasgow Warriors since 2018 and took over as managing director in 2025 following the departure of Al Kellock.

The 45-year-old will depart to take up a new opportunity with his family in Australia, leaving with the club in a strong position both on and off the pitch.

“Leaving Glasgow Warriors has been a very difficult decision for me to make,” said Brown.

“Over the last seven years, I have loved my time at the club. Growing up in the west of Scotland, I have always had a real passion and attachment to Glasgow Warriors which will stay with me forever.

“I am incredibly proud of what we have achieved during my time here. Glasgow Warriors is in a strong position, with a talented squad and a group of people working tirelessly behind the scenes to help the club succeed.

“It has been a real team effort, and I have relied on the support of our players, coaches, staff, commercial partners and supporters throughout my time here. I want to thank everyone for their commitment and hard work, and for making Glasgow Warriors such a special club to be part of.

“While I am excited about what lies ahead for my family and me, I will leave with enormous pride in what we have accomplished together and will always look back on my time at Glasgow Warriors with great affection.”

Brown joined Glasgow Warriors in 2018, having previously held roles with Scottish Rugby, sportscotland and Premiership Rugby.

He became Team Manager in 2019 before progressing to Head of Operations in 2021.

He was appointed interim Managing Director in September 2025 following Al Kellock’s departure to become Scottish Rugby Head of Performance Pathways, before being confirmed in the role on a permanent basis in March 2026.

Glasgow Warriors head coach Franco Smith said: “Kenny has been a tremendous support to me and the coaching team, and I have really valued the relationship we have built over the last few years.

“He understands the demands of professional rugby and the importance of creating the right environment for our players and staff to perform. He has always been committed to helping the team and the wider club achieve its ambitions, and I am grateful for everything he has done to support us.

“Of course, we are disappointed to be losing Kenny, but this is an exciting opportunity for him and his family, and we wish them every happiness as they begin this next chapter. He leaves with our very best wishes and with the respect and affection of everyone at the club.”

David White, the interim CEO of Scottish Rugby, added: “Kenny has made a significant contribution to Glasgow Warriors over many years, and his appointment as managing director was a natural progression following his outstanding service to the club in a number of roles.

“While we will be sorry to see Kenny leave, we are fully supportive of his decision and want to see our people take opportunities that are right for them and their families. That is an important part of the culture we want to build across Scottish Rugby, and we wish Kenny and his family every happiness as they start this next chapter.”

The club will work closely with Brown over the coming weeks to ensure a smooth transition ahead of his departure at the end of December.

Further details on the recruitment of a new managing director "will be communicated in due course" the club added.

title: Rory McIlroy on Bryson DeChambeau's future: Few options to continue playing competitive golf
article_text:
Rory McIlroy has become the face of European golf in recent years. This week, he is aiming to tie Colin Montgomerie for the most Race to Dubai titles at the DP World Tour Championship.

Playing on the DP World Tour on and off throughout his career and with a more consistent presence on the circuit over the last few seasons, McIlroy has seen firsthand the ebbs and flows of the league.

With LIV Golf 2.0 never getting off the ground and the , players who appeared ready to continue calling that circuit home are now looking for new playing ground.

The DP World Tour has become the likeliest place for the lot given the PGA Tour's policies. Players like Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton have already crossed party lines and returned to the DP World Tour as they wait to learn whether there will be any avenue for them to return to the PGA Tour in 2027.

Thanks to his win at the 2024 U.S. Open, Bryson DeChambeau has status on the DP World Tour for the upcoming season, though it is unknown if he plans to play. Keeping his hand close to his vest, DeChambeau recently released a statement saying he will compete in the Nedbank Golf Challenge in December and then assess his situation next year.

McIlroy was asked to weigh in about the 33-year-old's future playing possibilities.

"I think a name like Bryson DeChambeau and everything he brings with him, good and bad, he brings eyeballs, which is a good thing for tournaments," McIlroy said. "And honestly, look, I'm certainly not in his shoes, and nor would I ever want to be, but it doesn't seem like he's got many options. You know, if he wants to play competitive golf, it doesn't seem like he's got many options."

In May, DeChambeau contended that his schedule, one day, could consist of playing the four major championships and otherwise shooting videos for his YouTube channel, which has since surpassed 3 million subscribers.

DeChambeau's last competitive tournament was LIV Golf Indianapolis in August. Since then, the two-time U.S. Open champion has released seven new videos on his channel, ranging from challenges with Gary Player to encounters with the Amish.

In early 2026, DeChambeau was among the four players the PGA Tour targeted via the Returning Member Program. Aimed at DeChambeau, Rahm, Cameron Smith and Brooks Koepka, the pathway gave this quartet a window to return to the PGA Tour under strict stipulations with penalties. Only Koepka took the PGA Tour up on the offer as he got out of his contract with LIV Golf.

DeChambeau does not have as rosy a relationship with the Tour as Koepka, given his past actions. In 2022, DeChambeau was among 11 LIV Golf members to file a lawsuit against the PGA Tour, challenging the suspensions and the withholding of Player Impact Program (PIP) money. A year later, DeChambeau withdrew his name from the suit and continued with LIV Golf, where he has carried more than water the last four years.

title: LIV Golf: What next for Bryson DeChambeau? How YouTube star can boost major hopes with return to traditional men's tours
article_text:
LIV Golf: What next for Bryson DeChambeau? How YouTube star can boost major hopes with return to traditional men's tours

Former Ryder Cup captain Paul McGinley believes Bryson DeChambeau needs to return to golf’s traditional tours to boost his hopes of winning majors again.

DeChambeau's competitive future remains uncertain, following the demise of LIV Golf, with no pathway currently in place for an immediate return to the PGA Tour and no confirmation of how frequently he plans to tee it up in 2027.

The two-time major champion said in a statement on Sunday that he 'still believes in team golf', with the two-time US Open champion pledging to approach the next part of his career "with humility and respect."

He previous said he would focus on YouTube golf and "play tournaments that want him" if LIV Golf didn't survive, then recently revealed on the "Figuring Out" podcast that he hoped it 'exists forever' before the league entered the liquidation phase of bankruptcy.

On the possibility of YouTube golf becoming DeChambeau's focus going forward, McGinley told the Sky Sports Golf podcast: "You never know with Bryson, but I can see it. It would be a dumb move, to go from playing YouTube golf to trying to compete in majors.

"The longer Bryson stays away and off traditional platforms, the less chance he has of winning major championships going forward, because you cut your teeth in week-to-week PGA Tour and DP World Tour events before you elevate into these major championships.

"If you're cutting your teeth playing fun golf and LIV golf, it's a massive step up to then try and compete at the very top against the best players in the world - it's just not going to happen.

"You're training and preparing to win major championships at such a low level that you cannot step up in that way. If he does it [sticks with YouTube and team golf], I think it would pretty much close the door on him winning major championships during that period of time.

"If he comes back and plays the DP World Tour or the PGA Tour in the years to come, I think he could become a factor again winning majors, but not from LIV 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 and not even from YouTube golf."

DeChambeau was one of only two players to win a major while an active LIV Golf player, snatching the 2024 US Open before posting three top-10s in majors the following year, then missed the cut in the first three majors of 2026 as uncertainty grew over LIV Golf's future.

"With these guys who went to LIV, in the first couple of years they went, they were pretty competitive when it came to playing majors," McGinley explained. "The longer they stayed on LIV, the more disconnected they got from the top of the leaderboards in these majors.

"When Jon Rahm went to LIV, he was best player that Europe had in Italy in the Ryder Cup, the current Masters champion and one of the world's best. He went from that position to becoming a non-event when it comes to major championships.

"If you took money out of the equation and it was the same on LIV as it was on the PGA Tour and DP World Tour. If you said to each player 'which platform is going to give you the best opportunity to win major championships?', none of them would pick LIV.

"The reason they picked LIV and went on LIV was purely for financial reasons - it was not the ideal platform to prepare to win major championships."

DeChambeau is eligible to apply for DP World Tour membership for the 2027 season based on being a recent major champion, although has a November 15 deadline to confirm his position.

Sergio Garcia is among those to have their intention to return to the European circuit next year, having previously criticised the tour, with many DP World Tour players unhappy with the decision to welcome LIV Golf players back.

"Are all of these people coming back going to put 50 per cent back into the value of the tour in terms of the business model? Are sponsors suddenly going to be crawling over themselves to get involved with the DP World Tour? I don't think so," McGinley admitted.

"I'm not saying it's not great to have all the players back, but what is the end game here? The end game here is that the DP World Tour becomes more sustainable than already has been.

"Guy Kinnings [DP World Tour chief executive] will be in a very strong position in terms of where he gives these invites to, especially the guys who are not exempt and are trying to come back on the DP World Tour.

"He's got this balancing act of, yes, these guys from LIV do add somewhat of a value, but more importantly, he's got to firstly look after the guys who have played the DP World Tour for the last three, four, five years and who have remained loyal to that tour.

"There's also the young kids who have come through the HotelPlanner Tour, as well as DP World Tour's Q-school in the last couple of years, who have just got their status on the tour - they've got to be given real ample opportunity as well.

"Just because the big guys have come back to play, it can't be at their costs, so he's got this balancing act that he's going on. He understands as a member's organisation, he's got to be fair to the guys who stayed loyal, as well as the LIV guys coming back."

title: DP World Tour DQs player from Q-School for ‘serious misconduct’
article_text:
The DP World Tour disqualified a player for serious misconduct during Monday’s fourth round of its final stage of Q-School.

Frank Kennedy, a 21-year-old from Manchester, England, was tied for 28th at 15 under through 72 holes of the 108-hole tournament when he was disqualified for what DPWT officials described in a statement as “serious misconduct after causing deliberate damage to the course.”

Monday Q Info’s Ryan French reported the specifics after speaking to several sources who witnessed the behavior, saying Kennedy took a “1-foot divot” out of the 11th green. French added that Kennedy argued extensively in the scoring area after receiving his DQ.

Golf Channel has reached out directly to Kennedy and is awaiting comment.

Kennedy parred the hole, the par-5 11th at Infinitum Golf’s Hills Course, then double-bogeyed the next hole. Otherwise, he had put together a solid round, a 3-under 69 with seven birdies.

Kennedy’s DQ also moved the cut line from 12 under to 11 under, keeping tournaments alive for seven players: Luis Masaveu, Jerry Ji, Lukas Boandl, Haydn Barron, Jesper Sandborg, Antoine Pouguet and Philipp Katich.

The top 60 players and ties advanced to the final 36 holes, after which the top 15 and ties will received DPWT cards via Category 18. Everyone else who finishes 108 holes will earn some sort of HotelPlanner Tour status.

Italy’s Matteo Cristoni leads final stage at 24 under, a shot ahead of Josele Ballester and Marcus Helligkilde. Other notables currently inside the top 15 and ties include Cameron John (21 under), Ben An (20 under), Americans Joshua Lee (20 under) and Jhared Hack (19 under), and Tom Lewis (19 under).

Amateur Dean Greyserman, a recent Stanford grad, is among those within three shots of the cut line, as are Pablo Larrazabal, Edoardo Molinari and Cameron Adam.

Kennedy was an accomplished amateur, most notably winning the 2023 Lytham Trophy at 17 years old. He also made the semifinals of the British Amateur that summer and decided to turn professional later that year.

Two years ago, Kennedy became the third-youngest winner in HotelPlanner Tour history by capturing the Euram Bank Open. He played this past season on that tour, finishing No. 62 in points, meaning he has only Category 8 status on the HotelPlanner Tour for 2027.

He is currently ranked No. 777 in the Official World Golf Ranking.

title: Dustin Johnson’s agent reveals ‘wheels are in motion’ for major career move after LIV Golf collapse
article_text:
Dustin Johnson's agent has revealed the former World No.1 is already exploring his next career move following LIV Golf's collapse, insisting the two-time major champion remains hungry to compete at the highest level.

Speaking to golf reporter Bob Harig on The Daily Drive, Johnson's agent David Winkle offered a significant update on the American's future.

"Everything is a bit up in the air, but I can tell you he is pursuing paths toward the highest level of competition," Winkle said in a text message to Harig.

"Time will tell exactly what that looks like and entails, but the wheels are in motion."

Winkle also insisted the 42-year-old has no intention of retiring, adding: "Dustin is still very motivated and hungry to compete, so he has no intention of letting up. I'm actually very excited about the months ahead, wherever they may find him playing."

Johnson had been one of LIV Golf's biggest names since joining the breakaway league in 2022, reportedly receiving a signing bonus of around $150 million.

He subsequently collected approximately $65 million in prize money and bonuses, winning three individual titles and captaining 4Aces GC to the inaugural team championship in 2022.

However, the withdrawal of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund's reported $5 billion backing and the collapse of a proposed rescue deal involving BC Partners have left LIV facing liquidation.

Johnson had appeared willing to continue under a restructured LIV 2.0 model, but those plans have now fallen apart.

A return to the PGA Tour would appear to be one of Johnson's main options, although the two-time major champion faces a complicated route back.

He is currently subject to a 12-month suspension following his departure from LIV Golf, having last competed at the circuit's season-ending event in Indianapolis in August.

PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp has previously stressed the importance of enforcing the organisation's rules, suggesting an immediate return cannot be taken for granted.

Nevertheless, Johnson has a compelling case based on his career achievements.

The 42-year-old has won 24 PGA Tour titles, including the 2016 US Open and 2020 Masters, and sits sixth on the circuit's all-time money list with more than $75 million in career earnings.

His 24 victories on the PGA Tour have also traditionally provided lifetime membership status, so it remains to be seen what happens there.

Unlike some former LIV colleagues, Johnson did not publicly criticise the PGA Tour when he departed in 2022, potentially working in his favour should reinstatement eventually be considered.

The DP World Tour could provide Johnson with a more immediate opportunity to return to competitive golf.

The European circuit is reportedly opening the door to select DP World Tour appearances for former LIV players without category status in 2027.

GolfMagic understands from an insider that select invites for ex-LIV players with category status are not expected to feature Rolex Series events.

Johnson last appeared on the DP World Tour via an invite with a missed cut at the Hero Dubai Desert Classic at the end of January.

The former World No.1 also retains a lifetime exemption into The Masters following his 2020 victory at famed Augusta National, but his exemptions into the other three majors have now expired.

Johnson would need to either qualify or receive a special invite to compete in the PGA Championship, US Open and The Open in 2027.

There may also be a personal consideration behind Johnson's future plans.

The American has previously spoken about wanting a relatively short professional career so he can eventually become a 'sports dad'.

Married to Paulina Gretzky, daughter of ice hockey legend Wayne Gretzky, Johnson has two sons, Tatum and River, aged 11 and nine.

Spending more time supporting their sporting ambitions could become increasingly appealing as they grow older.

For now, however, Johnson appears far from ready to walk away from professional golf.

Winkle's comments suggest the 42-year-old remains motivated to compete and is determined to find another opportunity at the highest level.

title: PREM Champions Northampton pick up long-term injury during Test window
article_text:
Zimbabwe and Northampton prop Cleopas Kundiona will be out of action for the foreseeable future after breaking his arm whilst on international duty at the weekend.

The tight-head suffered the blow in the first half of Zimbabwe’s 43-7 defeat to Samoa in the fourth round of the World Rugby Nations Cup at Wakefield RL’s DIY Kitchen’s Stadium.

It was the 27-year-old’s 20th cap for the Sables, who have qualified for their first Rugby World Cup since 1991.

Kundiona, who made his Test debut as a 19-year-old in June 2018, will be expected to anchor the African side’s scrum in Australia next year.

He has become an important player for Northampton, too, with the 125kg former Natal player clocking up seven appearances for Saints in all competition this season, all of them starts.

Kundiona has enjoyed plenty of game time due to Trevor Davison’s prolonged absence from the front row.

Former England international Davison has undergone three knee operations in the last year and has not played for the club since the end of March.

Depending on his comeback date, Saints Director of Rugby Phil Dowson may look to bring in a replacement to cover Kundiona, as Sonny Tonga’uiha and Ion Neculai are his only other options at tight-head.

Other than the Kundiona blow, Sables boss Pieter Benade has confirmed to RugbyPass they have a clean bill of health heading into this weekend’s match against Uruguay in Ealing.

title: Scotland fly in forgotten scrum-half from France ahead of Wallabies Test
article_text:
Vastly experienced scrum-half Ali Price has replaced Gus Warr in Scotland’s training squad leading up to this weekend’s game against Australia at Murrayfield.

Otherwise, Scotland have no fresh updates to report in the wake of Saturday’s disappointing 43-21 defeat to New Zealand.

Warr has returned to his club side, Sale Sharks, after being involved in training ahead of the All Blacks game, while Price, who plays his club rugby for Montpellier in the Top 14, is now in line to win his 69th cap for his country.

The 33-year-old British and Irish Lions international was last capped by Scotland against Fiji two years ago, having made his debut against Georgia back in 2016.

Price has made seven appearances for Montpellier this season, starting in three of them.

He joins fellow Top 14 player Ben White and George Horne as scrum-half options, along with utility player Jamie Dobie, for the visit of the wounded Wallabies.

Scotland have won four of the last five fixtures between the teams, and the solitary defeat was by a single-point margin, Blair Kinghorn missing a last-gasp kick to overturn a 16-15 scoreline against them in 2022.

title: Ulster's Timoney 'grateful' for Ireland chances
article_text:
Ireland forward Nick Timoney says the patience he needed to show before becoming a regular part of Andy Farrell's matchday squads has made him more appreciative of his appearances in the green shirt.

Speaking to Gavin Andrews on BBC Sport NI's Ireland Rugby Social, external podcast, the Ulster back row explains that he thought he may never get the chance to prove himself on the international stage and is now relishing the prospect of trying to pin down a starting berth.

Timoney made his Ireland bow in a summer Test against the USA in 2021, being handed a chance to impress while others were on duty with the British and Irish Lions in South Africa.

Since then, the 31-year-old was habitually part of Farrell's extended squads but added only two caps to his tally in the subsequent four years, coming off the bench against Argentina a few months after his debut, and then scoring two tries against Fiji in November 2022.

An embarrassment of riches in the ultra-competitive back row positions meant he had to wait the bulk of three years for his next appearance, a summer tour victory over Georgia in 2025, followed by his fifth cap against Japan last autumn.

Something of a breakthrough year in 2026 has seen him feature in all nine of Ireland's games to date across the Six Nations and the Nations Championship, three as a starter and six as a replacement.

"It felt like a long time waiting for the chances I've gotten loads of now in the last 12 months," said Timoney.

"You feel like you're ready to take them but if they don't come it's hard to know and obviously the coaches have seen progression in me to some extent to start picking me.

"I'm grateful for it and trying not to think too big picture about it but it's certainly been a lot of fun and a great privilege as well, I'm very lucky to have been given the chance."

The consistent presence of the likes of back row regulars Caelan Doris, Josh van der Flier, Jack Conan and the now-retired Peter O'Mahony led to Timoney's opportunities being limited following his debut.

"When you're getting past 30 in rugby, it's not that you're finished...[Stuart] McCloskey is the shining example of that not being the case, that your bed's not totally made by the time you get to your later years in your career.

"It's certainly easy to think at 28 or 29 you're not really breaking through, it's not really going anywhere or felt like that maybe the chances don't come but luckily for me they have come and it's a testament to the coaches and whole set-up of Irish rugby that the door's not closed."

Timoney adds that he believes the waiting has made him savour his more regular involvement in recent times, including a starting role in Friday's win over Argentina.

"Before I'd have been desperate to get out there. It still is the be-all-and-end-all but you're better equipped...you've had brief glimpses and have also felt that it might not be coming back so going into games just feeling grateful and happy to be there and excited for the opportunity is the best way to do it and not just overcome by the pressure of it all but just enjoy the moments.

"If you do that, you'll play better so that's what I've been trying to do."

The challenge for Timoney now is to keep hold of the shirt, with a coveted place in the starting side for the much anticipated encounter with South Africa on 21 November likely to come down to a straight choice between him and former world player of the year Van der Flier.

First up though is a meeting with Fiji in Dublin on Saturday as the Irish target a fourth win from five games in the inaugural edition of the Nations Championship.

"There are good back rowers in my position, there's very good back rowers. That's always the plan - if you get a chance, you want to take it and give a good enough account of yourself that you get another chance.

"Fingers crossed I do this week but you never know. In the same way you wouldn't have expected to start last week. I wouldn't have expected to before so there's never assumptions to be made, you never come in thinking 'I'm a banker to play this week'.

"Fingers crossed I get another chance but it's very much one day at a time."

title: Kumamoto Masters Japan 2026 badminton: Treesa Jolly-Gayatri Gopichand in second round; Satwik-Chirag withdraw
DeChambeau running out of options
article_text:
Rory McIlroy says the addition of Bryson DeChambeau to the DP World Tour next season would bring more "eyeballs" to the tour but feels the American is running out of options.

DeChambeau's competitive future is uncertain following the collapse of LIV Golf, with the two-time US Open champion last week saying he will approach his next move with "humility and respect".

The 33-year-old American can apply for DP World Tour membership based on his status as a recent major champion, which would offer him the chance to earn back his PGA Tour card for 2028.

"I think a name like Bryson DeChambeau and everything he brings with him, good and bad, he brings eyeballs, which is a good thing for tournaments," said McIlroy, who was pipped to the 2024 US Open in dramatic fashion by DeChambeau.

"Honestly, I'm certainly not in his shoes, and nor would I ever want to be but it doesn't seem like he's got many options.

"You know, if he wants to play competitive golf, it doesn't seem like he's got many options."

Northern Ireland's McIlroy was speaking to reporters in Dubai before the DP World Tour Championship as he chases a record-equalling eighth season-long title.

The six-time major winner trails Spain's Eugenio Chacarra by 533 points in the Race to Dubai standings going into the final event in Dubai, which offers 2,000 points to the winner.

Nine players - Chacarra, McIlroy, Patrick Reed, Casey Jarvis, Aaron Rai, Jon Rahm, Ryan Fox, Jayden Schaper and Daniel Hillier - can still clinch the Race to Dubai title, but McIlroy would guarantee his fifth straight crown with victory at Jumeirah Golf Estates this week.

McIlroy's excellent record at the Dubai tournament includes three wins and a play-off defeat by England's Matt Fitzpatrick last year.

"I'm very excited to be back here, very excited to be in contention for the eighth," said the 37-year-old.

"I made some ground up last week, maybe not as much as I wanted, but I felt like it was a step in the right direction.

"Getting back to a place where I played, I played well and I had a lot of success, even last year in the play-off with Matt, it's been a course that's been very good to me over the years, and I have a lot of experience on it and a lot of experience up at the top end of the leaderboard."

An eighth Race to Dubai title would draw McIlroy alongside Colin Montgomerie, who won seven straight European Tour Order of Merit titles in the 1990s before adding an eighth in 2005.

With McIlroy chasing a fifth successive Race to Dubai title, he spoke about how proud he is of the "consistency" and "longevity" he has shown in his career.

"I think this will be the 15th or 16th year in a row that I will have finished the year in the top 10 in the world rankings," said the world number two.

"There may be a couple others that have done that before. Yeah, I'm very proud of that. I think that's maybe an underrated part of careers, is that longevity piece.

"I was very lucky to start so young and get my tour card at 18, and I've stayed pretty much injury-free throughout my career.

"And I've kept working and trying to get better at certain aspects of the game and always tried to see weaknesses or be critical of myself and try to get better at them."

title: All Blacks to rip up team and Wales legend to pull on boots again
article_text:
Here are your rugby evening headlines for Tuesday, November 10.

All Blacks coach Neil Barnes has confirmed that New Zealand are likely to rotate against Wales this weekend, with a couple of high-profile names already ruled out.

Prolific try-scorer Will Jordan has been ruled out with a 'minor tear' in his hamstring, while Jordie Barrett will also not feature - despite passing his HIA protocols after a head-on-head clash against Scotland that knocked a tooth loose.

On Jordan's involvement in the rest of the Nations Championship, Barnes said: "We are hopeful. At this stage, we're not conclusive where he's at.

"It's a minor tear, but depends how quickly it starts to heal this week, so we'll see how that progresses as the week comes on."

The coach also admitted that New Zealand could rotate from the side that beat Scotland in Murrayfield.

"There's a lot of positions in this team where it's really close," he said. "We can make quite a few changes, still put a damn good side in and there's a lot of trust in the people we've selected for this group.

"A couple of people will get opportunities and they deserve them. If they play, that raises the bar on that position and then the other person has got to raise his game to get back in. It's just the flow-on effect, really. There's areas there where we'll make a couple of changes."

Wales and Ospreys legend Justin Tipuric will pull on his boots again later this month in a special match to celebrate his career.

Some of the Ospreys' greatest names will take part, as a legends team take on Trebanos XV at St Helen's on Sunday, November 22. Proceeds from the match will go to Ospreys in the Community, as well as Trebanos - Tipuric's home club.

The three-time Lion grew up in Trebanos, playing his junior rugby at the club. His brother also played for them, while his father was once captain.

As a professional player, he made 229 appearances for the Ospreys between 2009 and 2025 - captaining the club for a number of years.

For Wales, he won 93 caps, while he appeared on three Lions tours. He has moved into the Ospreys' coaching group since retiring.

"Trebanos is where it all started for me, so to bring the Ospreys and my home club together on the same pitch means a lot," said Tipuric. "I’ve been lucky to share a changing room with some brilliant players and people over the years, and it’ll be special to have so many of them back together.

"I’m hoping it’ll be a great day for everyone involved, whatever the legs can still manage! Trebanos gave me so much growing up, so it’s great to be able to give something back to the club."

Some of the legends involved are set to be announced in the coming days, with the Ospreys' head of rugby, Dan Griffiths, paying tribute to Tipuric.

"Justin is one of the greatest players to wear the black jersey," he said. "He was a world-class player and an even better person, but above all, a humble, homegrown Osprey who never forgot where he came from.

"This match is a chance for supporters to come together and say thank you, and there’s no better way to do that than by bringing together the two clubs that mean so much to him.

"We’d encourage everyone to get their tickets early and be part of what promises to be a fantastic occasion."

Montpellier scrum-half Ali Price has been called up to train with the Scotland squad to replace Gus Warr, who has returned to Sale.

Price, 33, last played for Scotland against Fiji in November 2024, but has been drafted in by Gregor Townsend following some impressive displays in the Top 14 this season, with Montpellier sitting third.

Following the demoralising 43-21 Nations Championship defeat to New Zealand, Scotland will look to produce a response against Australia at Murrayfield on Sunday.

Ben White started at scrum-half against the All Blacks, with George Horne taking over for the closing stages. Jamie Dobie, who can also play at number nine, was deployed on the wing.

Following the game against the Wallabies, Scotland will then face Japan on November 21 ahead of the Nations Championship finals weekend at Twickenham.

title: WTA expands merchandise business with TOGETHXR collaboration and Monarch Commerce partnership
article_text:
The WTA (Women’s Tennis Association) is expanding its new official merchandise business with a TOGETHXR collaboration and a partnership with Monarch Commerce to develop its first dedicated online fan shop.

Building on the previously announced collaboration with the iconic Hello Kitty ®, these latest agreements mark the next phase of a WTA initiative to connect women’s tennis with sport, style and popular culture, while creating new ways for fans to engage beyond the court.

The TOGETHXR "Everyone Watches Women’s Tennis" T-shirt line launched on-site at the 2026 FAGE WTA Finals in Indian Wells and is now available online at TOGETHXR.com, bringing the fastest-growing and most engaging women’s sports media and commerce brand into the WTA’s first official merchandise offering.

Co-founded by athletes Alex Morgan, Sue Bird, Simone Manuel and Chloe Kim alongside sports media veteran Jessica Robertson, TOGETHXR champions women’s stories at the intersection of sport, lifestyle and culture. The company behind the “Everyone Watches Women’s Sports™” slogan has built a community around increasing the visibility and representation of women in sport.

"We saw huge demand for the ‘Everyone Watches Women’s Tennis’ T-shirt in the Fan Village over opening weekend in Indian Wells,” said Sarah Swanson, Chief Brand Officer at WTA Ventures. “TOGETHXR has given fans a simple, bold way to show their pride in women’s sport, and it’s been brilliant to see tennis fans make that message their own. That’s the kind of response we want to build on with Monarch Commerce as we give fans more ways to shop for WTA merchandise year-round.”

Bailey Williamson, Senior Vice President of Partnerships at TOGETHXR, said: "Women’s tennis has always been a powerful force in sport and culture, driven by athletes who transcend the court and a global fanbase whose passion is undeniable. At TOGETHXR, we believe fandom is something you wear, share and celebrate. Partnering with the WTA to bring ‘Everyone Watches Women’s Tennis’ to life is an opportunity to celebrate the athletes, the fans and the cultural influence of a sport that continues to set the standard.”

To support the next stage of its retail business, WTA has finalized an agreement with Monarch Commerce, a boutique merchandise and e-commerce business originating from Monarch Collective, the first investment fund focused exclusively on women’s sports, co-founded by Jasmine Robinson and Kara Nortman.

Monarch Commerce, whose client roster includes the WNBA’s Atlanta Dream and Just Women’s Sports, brings a dedicated understanding of women’s sports audiences, combining brand storytelling, fan insights, product development and physical and digital retail expertise to maximize revenue, profitability and brand impact for women’s sports teams, leagues, athletes and the broader ecosystem.

The partnership will support the development and launch of the WTA’s first dedicated online fan shop, expected to go live in Spring 2027. The shop will give supporters a new way to purchase official WTA products, including Hello Kitty and TOGETHXR throughout the year.

Sarah Swanson added: “Monarch Commerce understands women’s sports and the fans driving their growth. That expertise will help us build on our first collections with products fans want to wear and help us create an elevated retail experience that brings them closer to the WTA. The possibilities here are really exciting.”

Sam Bushy, CEO, Monarch Commerce, said: “Monarch Commerce is honored to partner with the WTA to bring its ecommerce and product vision to life for fans. The WTA has long been a groundbreaking force in women’s sports, shaping the game and inspiring generations of fans. We are excited to create new ways for both long time and new fans to celebrate the sport they love through merchandise that honors its heritage, captures its spirit, and reflects their own personal style.”

The expansion forms part of WTA Ventures’ strategy to build the long-term commercial value of women’s tennis. By developing new products, partnerships and routes to market, WTA Ventures aims to deepen fan engagement, reach new audiences and create additional revenue opportunities that support the sport’s continued growth.

Fans will be able to purchase the TOGETHXR T-shirt line and previously announced Hello Kitty merchandise in the Fan Village at the 2026 FAGE WTA Finals, Indian Wells, which runs from 8 to 15 November. The full Hello Kitty collection will also be available online at Sanrio.com.

Further details of the online shop and future collections will be announced ahead of the anticipated Spring 2027 launch.

title: Badminton: Treesa-Gayatri stun higher-ranked Japanese pair to enter Kumamoto Masters pre-quarters
article_text:
New Delhi [India], November 10 (ANI): India's Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand advanced to the women's doubles pre-quarterfinals at the Kumamoto Masters Japan 2026 after defeating higher-ranked Japanese pair Hinata Suzuki and Nao Yamakita in straight games on Tuesday, according to Olympics.com.

The second game was more one-sided, with Treesa and Gayatri maintaining their dominance to register a 21-14 victory and seal their place in the next round. The Indian duo will next face third seeds and world No. 5 Japanese pair Rin Iwanaga and Kie Nakanishi in the round of 16.

title: Asian Games champion An dominates BWF world rankings
article_text:
Seoul, Korea, November 10, 2026: Korea’s Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games badminton champion An Se-young underlined her dominance of the world game by winning her 11th international title of the year on Sunday, Yonhap News reports.

An, world No. 1, defeated second-ranked Akane Yamaguchi of Japan 2-1 (21-12, 15-21, 21-16) in the women's singles final at Yeosu Victor Korea Open at Jinnam Stadium in Yeosu.

This was An's 11th international victory of the year, tying the record first set by the men's singles player Kento Momota of Japan in 2019 and equaled by An herself in 2025.

This year, An has won eight tournaments on the BWF World Tour and gold medals at the Badminton Asia Championships, BWF World Championships and Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.

An has lost just once in 72 matches all season - the lone defeat coming against Wang Zhiyi of China in the All-England Open final in March.

An also extended her winning streak against world No. 2 Yamaguchi to 11 matches.

An, who previously won the Korea Open in 2022 and 2023, said she became emotional in the final hearing rousing cheers from Korean fans.

"I felt so happy knowing there are so many badminton fans here," An said of a sellout crowd of 3,500.

"It is always great to win on home soil. I even got goose bumps hearing their cheers. I would like to thank these fans for their support. Sometimes, during a match, I get discouraged when I make mistakes. But these fans helped me play with confidence even after errors."

On winning 11 titles in back-to-back seasons, An said, "I am proud of myself for this accomplishment.

"I think I have grown up mentally from last year," she added. "I have also learned how to turn things around when I am running on fumes."

An will take some time off before the BWF World Tour Finals, starting December 9 in Hangzhou, China.

title: PTPA Blames Tennis Calendar for Rybakina’s WTA Finals Withdrawal
article_text:
The Professional Tennis Players Association (PTPA) renewed its attack on the tennis calendar on Monday, saying world number one Elena Rybakina pulled out of the WTA Finals because “her body had nothing left to give.” The criticism adds pressure on the tours over player workload.

Rybakina withdrew on Saturday, a day before the season-ending event began at Indian Wells. In a statement, the 27-year-old said she had enjoyed an incredible season but that her body was not physically ready to compete. Organisers gave a viral illness as the reason.

The withdrawal was not a complete surprise. Rybakina had moved her pre-tournament news conference back by a day and had already pulled out of the Pan Pacific Open quarterfinals in Tokyo last month with a neck injury. Marta Kostyuk took her place in Group 1.

The Kazakh finishes 2026 with a 54-14 record and four titles: the Australian Open, Stuttgart, the US Open and Ningbo. She secured the year-end number one ranking while in Tokyo, and she was due to defend the title she won unbeaten in Riyadh last year.

The PTPA used her season to make its point. In a social media post, the group noted that she had won two Grand Slam titles and four titles overall, yet still arrived at the final event of the year with nothing left.

“Players shouldn’t reach the biggest event of the year running on empty,” the association said. It added that it would keep pushing for a season that leaves players healthy enough to finish it.

The WTA did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. The tour has said before that athlete welfare is a top priority and that it has listened to players’ views on the calendar.

The debate extends to the men’s game. American Taylor Fritz, the top seed at this week’s Stockholm Open, said on Sunday that the short off-season gives players almost no chance to recover.

Speaking on “The Running Interview Show,” Fritz said the tour is year-round and that players get a one-month break at most. He explained that taking the full month off would mean starting the new season without practice, so in reality players can rest for about two weeks before training again. “You are literally living out of a suitcase,” he said.

The ATP has said players keep control over their own schedules and that it is working on incentives to encourage a suitable number of matches across the season.

Schedule complaints are central to the PTPA’s broader battle with the sport’s governing bodies. The association was founded in 2020 by Novak Djokovic and Vasek Pospisil. In March 2025 it filed an antitrust lawsuit against the ATP, WTA, International Tennis Federation and International Tennis Integrity Agency in New York, London and Brussels, citing the 11-month calendar alongside pay and playing conditions.

The case has evolved since. The ITF and ITIA were dropped as defendants in September 2025, and Tennis Australia reached a settlement with the PTPA in January this year. Djokovic stepped away from the organisation that same month, saying his values no longer matched its direction. The ATP and WTA continue to reject the lawsuit’s claims.

Top players have also spoken out separately. Carlos Alcaraz and Aryna Sabalenka have both called for the number of mandatory tournaments to be cut.

title: Japan Masters 2026 Starts Today, 11 Indonesian Representatives Ready to Compete, Check the Schedule and Opponents
article_text:
KUMAMOTO, Aktualita.co - The Kumamoto Japan Masters 2026 badminton tournament officially enters its first day on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. A total of 11 Indonesian representatives are preparing to face the competition in the BWF World Tour Super 500 event, which will take place at the Kumamoto Prefectural Gymnasium, Japan, until Sunday, November 15, 2026.

The Japan Masters 2026 is one of the important tournaments leading up to the end of this season's BWF World Tour. In addition to competing for a total prize pool of 500,000 US dollars, the players also have the opportunity to collect world ranking points.

Indonesia is relying on a number of seeded players, including Fajar Alfian/Muhammad Shohibul Fikri in the men's doubles sector, Putri Kusuma Wardani in women's singles, as well as Alwi Farhan and Moh. Zaki Ubaidillah in men's singles.

However, the preparation of the Merah Putih squad underwent changes after the All Indonesia Badminton Association (PBSI) withdrew two pairs from the participant list.

With these changes, Indonesia now has 11 representatives spread across five competition sectors.

The Japan Masters 2026 will last for six days, with matches starting from the qualifying round and the first round on Tuesday (10/11/2026).

Based on the organizer's schedule, the first day's matches are scheduled to start at 09:00 Japan time or 08:00 WITA.

- Tuesday, November 10, 2026: Qualifying and round of 32.

- Wednesday, November 11, 2026: Continuation of the round of 32.

- Thursday, November 12, 2026: Round of 16.

- Friday, November 13, 2026: Quarter-finals.

- Saturday, November 14, 2026: Semi-finals.

- Sunday, November 15, 2026: Finals for all sectors.

The quarter-final and semi-final matches are scheduled to start at 09:00 WITA, while the final matches on Sunday will start at 10:00 WITA.

The schedule for each player may change according to the order of matches, court conditions, and the duration of previous matches.

Indonesia is fielding a mix of young players and experienced athletes in this tournament.

In the men's singles sector, attention is focused on Alwi Farhan, who is scheduled to face Chinese Taipei representative Lin Chun-Yi in the opening match.

The duel is expected to be tight because both players have attacking abilities and rely on a fast-paced game.

Meanwhile, Moh. Zaki Ubaidillah, familiarly known as Ubed, will face Brian Yang from Canada. Meanwhile, Muhamad Yusuf must pass the qualifying round first by facing Yoo Tae-bin from South Korea.

In the women's singles sector, Indonesia only has one representative, namely Putri Kusuma Wardani. She is scheduled to meet the host player, Riko Gunji, in the first round.

The men's doubles sector is one of Indonesia's mainstays through Fajar Alfian/Muhammad Shohibul Fikri, who are the second seeds.

Fajar/Fikri will face Hiroki Okamura/Kyohei Yamashita from Japan. Meanwhile, Sabar Karyaman Gutama/Moh Reza Pahlevi Isfahani will meet the Chinese pair, Hu Ke Yuan/Liang Wei Keng.

In the women's doubles sector, Indonesia is relying on Febriana Dwipuji Kusuma/Meilysa Trias Puspitasari and Amallia Cahaya Pratiwi/Siti Fadia Silva Ramadhanti.

Febriana/Meilysa are scheduled to meet Chang Ching Hui/Yang Ching Tun from Chinese Taipei. Meanwhile, Tiwi/Fadia will face Rui Hirokami/Sayaka Hobara from Japan.

Meanwhile, three Indonesian pairs are appearing in the mixed doubles sector.

Amri Syahnawi/Nita Violina Marwah will face Ruben Garcia/Lucia Rodriguez from Spain. Marwan Faza/Aisyah Salsabila Putri Pranata will meet Yuta Watanabe/Maya Taguchi from Japan.

Another pair, Dejan Ferdinansyah/Felisha Alberta Nathaniel Pasaribu, is scheduled to face Gao Jia Xuan/Wu Meng Ying from China.

Ahead of the start of the Japan Masters 2026, PBSI decided to cancel the participation of two pairs, namely Devin Artha Wahyudi/Ali Faathir Rayhan and Rachel Allessya Rose/Febi Setianingrum.

The decision was taken after the coaching team evaluated the performance and readiness of the athletes following the series of tournaments in Europe.

Head Coach of Indonesian Men's Doubles, Antonius Budi Ariantho, explained that Devin/Faathir need additional time to improve their performance before returning to international competition.

"We withdrew Devin/Faathir's participation from the Kumamoto Masters 2026 because the evaluation from the three previous tournaments in Europe showed results that were not good enough," said Antonius, Monday (9/11/2026).

The pair is subsequently directed to undergo training in preparation for the Hong Kong Open and the Syed Modi India International 2026.

Meanwhile, Rachel/Febi are considered not yet in an ideal condition to return to competition.

Head Coach of PBSI Women's Doubles, Karel Mainaky, chose to provide time for improvement at the Cipayung National Training Center so that the pair can prepare themselves for the next competition season.

The withdrawal of the two pairs reduced the number of Indonesian representatives from the initial plan of 13 to 11 participants.

The attention of Indonesian badminton fans is also focused on Fajar Alfian/Muhammad Shohibul Fikri.

Their status as the second seeds makes the pair one of the candidates to be reckoned with in the fight for the men's doubles title.

However, the competition will not be easy because a number of strong pairs from China, South Korea, and Japan are also enlivening the tournament.

In women's singles, Putri Kusuma Wardani faces her own challenges as the only Indonesian representative.

Meanwhile, Alwi Farhan and Moh. Zaki Ubaidillah have the opportunity to show the development of their game when facing opponents with international experience.

The Japan Masters also holds important records for Indonesia.

Gregoria Mariska Tunjung won the women's singles sector in the inaugural edition in 2023. A year later, Fajar Alfian/Muhammad Rian Ardianto won the men's doubles title in the 2024 edition.

Western Bulldogs Secure Platinum Partnership Extension with Greenworks Australia
article_text:
The Western Bulldogs have officially secured a three-year partnership extension with Greenworks Australia, locking in the global outdoor equipment manufacturer as a Platinum Partner through to the end of the 2029 AFL season.

The renewed agreement builds upon an inaugural 2026 campaign that saw Greenworks integrate into the club’s commercial framework and fan engagement channels.

As a global brand specialising in battery-powered outdoor power equipment and electric lifestyle vehicles, including lawnmowers, zero-turn commercial mowers, off-road go-karts, minibikes, and e-bikes, Greenworks will continue to leverage the Bulldogs’ domestic platform to drive market penetration across consumer, prosumer, and commercial sectors across Australia.

Highlighting the commercial returns achieved during the partnership’s opening year, Western Bulldogs chief commercial and strategy officer, Kon Karavias, said: “We’ve achieved a great deal with Greenworks and the team in the first year of this partnership, so we’re thrilled to be extending that into the future.”

“We look forward to building on that momentum and further strengthening our connection while rewarding our members and fans,” Karavias said.

Emphasising the brand’s commitment to expanding its footprint across the Western Bulldogs community, Greenworks Australia managing director, Adam Duggan, said: “We’ve seen some fantastic results from our first year partnering with the Western Bulldogs and are excited to build on that success over the next three years.”

“We’re passionate about supporting the teams and fans wherever we can, so we’re looking forward to finding even more ways to get involved and give back to the Western Bulldogs community.

“Keep an eye out at Western Bulldogs home games and across the Club’s social channels over the coming seasons – we’ve got plenty more planned,” Duggan said.

title: Aryna Sabalenka makes major team changes as two cut before WTA Finals – report
article_text:
Aryna Sabalenka has reportedly stopped working with former top-20 player Max Mirnyi as part of a wider shake-up of her team prior to the WTA Finals.

Sabalenka has endured a difficult 2026, including losing the No 1 ranking to Elena Rybakina and going slamless for the first time since 2023.

The 28-year-old hasn’t won a title on Tour since late March at the Miami Open, and this year she has endured a number of puzzling defeats from winning positions.

After suffering back-to-back early losses in the Asian Swing, journalist Ben Rothenberg claims that the Belarusian is no longer working with compatriot and coach Mirnyi.

The 49-year-old joined her coaching setup, which includes head coach Anton Dubrov and performance coach Jason Stacy, in the summer of 2025, with Mirnyi being on board for her US Open win last year.

However, he was not spotted on site at Indian Wells over the past week, and the former world No 18 wasn’t there for Sabalenka’s straight-sets win over Karolina Muchova at the WTA Finals on Monday.

When asked about what Mirnyi brought to her team, she told journalist Christian’s Court, “He is not here at Indian Wells with us, but Max has always been a great supporter.

“He would always message and give his advice, and yeah, having someone who was, I feel like, almost invisible or really number one in doubles to help me with that net approach, it’s really important. He’d been mostly focusing on my game at the net, and we’re trying to improve that.”

Rothenberg added that Mirnyi, who previously worked with Kei Nishikori, had “nothing to say” regarding a possible split from Sabalenka, who has also reportedly cut ties with physiotherapist and athletic trainer Helen Murawska.

Sabalenka started this year with a 23-1 record, as she reached the Australian Open final, before winning back-to-back titles at Indian Wells and Miami.

Since then, though, the world No 2 has chalked up a win-loss ratio of 25-10, with some of the high-profile defeats including a collapse against Diana Shnaider at the French Open and being bageled by Jessica Pegula in Berlin.

Despite that, she will hope her win over Muchova will provide an extra confidence boost ahead of round-robin matches against French Open champion Mirra Andreeva and Elina Svitolina.
